RULE 128: In VS-mode, attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA instruction or to access satp when hstatus.VTVM=1 cause mcause to be set to the virtual-instruction exception code 22.
RULE 129: When an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to the defined priority order is the one whose code is written into mcause.
RULE 130: An Instruction address breakpoint (exception code 3) has the highest priority among synchronous exceptions and therefore is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 131: During instruction address translation, the first encountered page fault (exception code 12), guest-page fault (exception code 20), or access fault (exception code 1) has priority over lower-priority exceptions and is reported in mcause.
RULE 132: An Instruction access fault with a physical address (exception code 1) has priority over illegal-instruction exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 133: An Illegal instruction exception (exception code 2) has priority over virtual-instruction exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 134: A Virtual instruction exception (exception code 22) has priority over instruction address misaligned exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 135: An Instruction address misaligned exception (exception code 0) has priority over environment-call exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 136: Environment call exceptions (exception codes 8, 9, 10, or 11) have priority over environment-break exceptions and are reported in mcause when they occur.
RULE 137: An Environment break exception (exception code 3) has priority over load/store/AMO address breakpoint exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 138: A Load/store/AMO address breakpoint exception (exception code 3) has priority over optional load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 139: Optional load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) have priority over explicit memory-access page-fault or access-fault exceptions and are reported in mcause when they occur.
RULE 140: During address translation for an explicit memory access, the first encountered page fault (exception code 13), guest-page fault (exception code 15), or access fault (exception codes 21 or 23) has priority over load/store/AMO access-fault exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 141: Load/store/AMO access-fault exceptions (exception codes 5 or 7) have priority over load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions when no higher-priority exception is present and are reported in mcause.
RULE 142: If no higher-priority exception applies, load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) are reported in mcause.
RULE 143: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the mcause CSR.
RULE 144: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the mcause CSR together with the mepc, mtval, mtval2, and mtinst CSRs.

NUMBER: 0x306

EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind
RULE 1: The mcounteren CSR has machine-mode read-write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counters, which continue to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 3: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the corresponding counter register (cycle, time, instret, or hpmcountern) while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 4: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is set, access to the corresponding counter register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 5: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to access the stimecmp or vstimecmp register while executing in any mode less privileged than M must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the stimecmp or vstimecmp register is permitted in S-mode if S-mode is implemented.
RULE 7: If the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the vstimecmp register via the stimecmp address is permitted in VS-mode if VS-mode is implemented and the TM bit in hcounteren does not otherwise prevent it.
RULE 8: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and all of its fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 9: In harts that implement U-mode, a zero value in an mcounteren field indicates that reads of the corresponding counter in a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: In harts that do not implement U-mode, the mcounteren register should not exist.
RULE 11: The mcounteren register permits M-mode to grant the next-lower privilege mode read access to selected hardware counters.
RULE 12: If the Smcdeleg or Ssccfg extensions are enabled (menvcfg.CDE = 1), then the mcounteren register additionally permits M-mode to delegate selected counters to S-mode.
RULE 13: A counter i is delegated when both mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 14: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1) and siselect holds the value 0x40 + i, the register state associated with counter i may be read via sireg.
RULE 15: When a counter i is delegated (mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1) and siselect holds the value 0x40 + i, the register state associated with counter i may be written via sireg.
RULE 16: While executing in M-mode or S-mode and with siselect containing a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access a sireg when siselect = 0x41 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: While executing in M-mode or S-mode and with siselect containing a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access a sireg when the selected counter is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding mcounteren bit = 0) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: Setting a bit in mcounteren does not affect whether the corresponding bit in scounteren is writable.
RULE 19: U-mode may only access a counter if the corresponding bits in scounteren and mcounteren are both set.
RULE 20: Read access to a scountovf bit X in S-mode is governed by the same mcounteren CSR that mediates access to the hpmcounter CSRs for that privilege mode.
RULE 21: Read access to a scountovf bit X in VS-mode is governed by both the mcounteren CSR and the hcounteren CSR that mediate access to the hpmcounter CSRs for that privilege mode.
RULE 22: In M-mode, the mcounteren register does not restrict read access to a scountovf bit X, which is always readable.
RULE 23: In S-mode and HS-mode, a scountovf bit X is readable only when the corresponding bit X in the mcounteren register is set; otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 24: In VS-mode, a scountovf bit X is readable only when both the corresponding bit X in the mcounteren register and the corresponding bit X in the hcounteren register are set; otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 25: If the CY bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the CY bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the cycle register.
RULE 26: If the TM bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the TM bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the time register.
RULE 27: If the IR bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the IR bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the instret register.
RULE 28: If an HPM n bit in hcounteren is clear, V=1, and the same HPM n bit in mcounteren is 1, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to read the hpmcounter n register.
RULE 29: If the TM bit in hcounteren is clear, VS-mode is active, and the TM bit in mcounteren is set, then a virtual-instruction exception occurs on an attempt to access the vstimecmp register via stimecmp.
RULE 30: If the TM bit in hcounteren and the TM bit in mcounteren are both set, and the implementation provides the vstimecmp register, then access to vstimecmp in VS-mode is permitted.
RULE 31: In VS-mode, an attempt to access a non-high-half counter CSR when the corresponding bit in hcounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception (exception code 22).
RULE 32: In VU-mode, an attempt to access a non-high-half counter CSR when the corresponding bit in either hcounteren or scounteren is 0 and the same bit in mcounteren is 1 raises a virtual-instruction exception (exception code 22).

REGISTER: mcountinhibit
NUMBER: 0x320
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mcountinhibit CSR is a machine-level CSR.
RULE 2: The mcountinhibit CSR has read/write privilege, designated MRW.
RULE 3: Settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only whether the counters increment and do not affect the counters' accessibility.
RULE 4: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the corresponding mcycle, minstret, or mhpmcounter n register increments as usual.
RULE 5: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the corresponding counter does not increment.
RULE 6: If the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared between those harts and writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts.
RULE 7: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were set to zero.
RULE 8: The mcountinhibit mechanism does not inhibit the mtime counter, which may be shared between multiple cores.
RULE 9: For any hardware counter that is delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the mcountinhibit register can be read and written via the scountinhibit register.
RULE 10: For any hardware counter that is not delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the scountinhibit register reads as zero, indicating that the associated mcountinhibit bit is not accessible through scountinhibit.
RULE 11: If the CDE field of the menvcfg CSR is zero, any attempt to access the scountinhibit register, which aliases mcountinhibit, causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When supervisor counter delegation is enabled, any attempt to access the scountinhibit register from VS-mode or VU-mode, which maps to mcountinhibit, raises a virtual-instruction exception.

REGISTER: mcycle
NUMBER: 0xb00
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: Implicit reads of the mcycle CSR are ordered as device input.
RULE 2: For the purposes of the FENCE instruction, a read of the mcycle CSR is classified as device input (I).
RULE 3: For the purposes of the FENCE instruction, a write of the mcycle CSR is classified as device output (O).
RULE 4: An explicit read of the mcycle CSR returns the mcycle state before the execution of the instruction.
RULE 5: An explicit write to the mcycle CSR suppresses and overrides any implicit writes or modifications to the same CSR by the same instruction.
RULE 6: CSR accesses, including accesses to the mcycle CSR, are weakly ordered by default, and other harts or devices may observe mcycle CSR accesses in an order different from program order.
RULE 7: The mcycle CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 8: The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running.
RULE 9: After a hart reset, the mcycle register contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 10: The mcycle register can be written with a given value.
RULE 11: Any write to the mcycle CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 12: The cycle CSR is a read-only shadow of mcycle.
RULE 13: Reading mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 14: Writing mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 15: The mcycle counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 16: If the CY bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the cycle CSR executed in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception, preventing read access to mcycle in those modes.
RULE 17: In harts that implement U-mode, each field of mcounteren is WARL and may be hardwired to zero, which causes reads of the corresponding counter - including reads of mcycle via the cycle CSR - to raise an illegal-instruction exception when executed in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 18: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mcycle register increments as usual.
RULE 19: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mcycle register does not increment.
RULE 20: The mcycle CSR may be shared between harts on the same core, and in that case the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared so writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts.
RULE 21: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were set to zero, causing the mcycle register to increment as usual.
RULE 22: The setting of the mcountinhibit register controls only the incrementing of the mcycle register and does not affect its accessibility.
RULE 23: If the MINH field (bit 62) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 24: If the SINH field (bit 61) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 25: If the UINH field (bit 60) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 26: If the VSINH field (bit 59) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 27: If the VUINH field (bit 58) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in VU-mode is inhibited.
RULE 28: When all INH bits (bits 62-58) of mcyclecfg are zero, counting of events for mcycle is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit (bits 61-58) of mcyclecfg is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero, thereby having no effect on mcycle counting.
RULE 30: If the Smcdeleg or Ssccfg extensions are implemented, supervisor-level code may access mcyclecfg, allowing it to influence mcycle counting behavior.
RULE 31: The mcycle register increments at the same rate as the elapsed cycle counter (CtrCycleCounter).

REGISTER: medeleg
NUMBER: 0x302
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 23..23=SGPF, 22..22=VI, 21..21=LGPF, 20..20=IGPF, 15..15=SPF, 13..13=LPF, 12..12=IPF, 11..11=EM, 10..10=EVS, 9..9=ES, 8..8=EU, 7..7=SAF, 6..6=SAM, 5..5=LAF, 4..4=LAM, 3..3=B, 2..2=II, 1..1=IAF, 0..0=IAM
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The medeleg CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege, meaning it can be read and written in Machine mode.
RULE 2: medeleg is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: In harts that implement S-mode, medeleg must exist.
RULE 4: Setting a bit in medeleg delegates the corresponding trap, when occurring in S-mode or U-mode, to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 5: In harts that do not implement S-mode, medeleg should not exist.
RULE 6: Implementations shall not have any bits of medeleg be read-only one; any synchronous trap that can be delegated must support not being delegated.
RULE 7: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, scause is written with the trap cause.
RULE 8: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, sepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 9: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, stval is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 10: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPP field of mstatus is written with the active privilege mode at the time of the trap.
RULE 11: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPIE field of mstatus is written with the value of the SIE field at the time of the trap.
RULE 12: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SIE field of mstatus is cleared.
RULE 13: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mcause is not written.
RULE 14: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mepc is not written.
RULE 15: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mtval is not written.
RULE 16: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPP field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 17: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPIE field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 18: medeleg has a bit position allocated for every synchronous exception, with the index of the bit equal to the value returned in the mcause register.
RULE 19: Setting bit 8 in medeleg allows user-mode environment calls to be delegated to a lower-privilege trap handler.
RULE 20: Bits in medeleg that correspond to exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes shall be read-only zero.
RULE 21: medeleg[11] is read-only zero.
RULE 22: medeleg[16] is read-only zero.
RULE 23: By default all traps at any privilege level are handled in M-mode, but the medeleg CSR can be used by M-mode to delegate selected traps to HS-mode.
RULE 24: A synchronous trap that has been delegated to HS-mode using medeleg is further delegated to VS-mode when V = 1 before the trap and the corresponding hedeleg bit is set.
RULE 25: Under the control of the CSR medeleg, guest-page-fault traps may be delegated from M-mode to HS-mode.
RULE 26: Guest-page-fault traps cannot be delegated to any privilege mode other than HS-mode via the CSR medeleg.
RULE 27: When a trap occurs in HS-mode or U-mode, the trap is taken in M-mode unless medeleg (or mideleg) delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in HS-mode.
RULE 28: When a trap occurs in VS-mode or VU-mode, the trap is taken in M-mode unless medeleg (or mideleg) delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in HS-mode unless hedeleg (or hideleg) further delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in VS-mode.

REGISTER: menvcfg
NUMBER: 0x30a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=STCE, 62..62=PBMTE, 61..61=ADUE, 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: Svnapot, Svpbmt
RULE 1: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg equals 00 then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 2: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg equals 01 then the instruction executes and performs a flush operation.
RULE 3: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg is not 01 and is not 00 then the instruction executes and performs an invalidate operation.
RULE 4: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 5: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is true then the instruction executes.
RULE 6: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 7: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is true then the instruction executes.
RULE 8: The CBIE, CBCFE, and CBZE fields in menvcfg do not affect the read or write behavior of the same-named fields in senvcfg or henvcfg.
RULE 9: The menvcfg CSR is a machine-level CSR.
RULE 10: The menvcfg CSR has read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 11: The menvcfgh CSR, which supplies the upper 32 bits of menvcfg, is a machine-level CSR with read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 12: The menvcfg CSR is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 13: If the FIOM bit is set to one in menvcfg, FENCE instructions executed in modes less privileged than M are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O also orders main memory accesses.
RULE 14: If FIOM=1 in menvcfg, for modes less privileged than M an atomic instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O and has its aq and/or rl bit set is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.
RULE 15: If S-mode is not supported or if satp.MODE is read-only zero, an implementation may make the FIOM bit read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 16: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the PI bit in a FENCE instruction implies predecessor device input and memory reads.
RULE 17: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the PO bit in a FENCE instruction implies predecessor device output and memory writes.
RULE 18: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the SI bit in a FENCE instruction implies successor device input and memory reads.
RULE 19: When FIOM=1 in menvcfg, setting the SO bit in a FENCE instruction implies successor device output and memory writes.
RULE 20: The PBMTE bit in menvcfg controls whether the Svpbmt extension is available for use in S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 21: When PBMTE=1 in menvcfg, Svpbmt is available for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 22: When PBMTE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented.
RULE 23: If Svpbmt is not implemented, the PBMTE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 24: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.
RULE 25: After changing menvcfg.PBMTE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' PBMT fields.
RULE 26: The ADUE bit in menvcfg controls whether hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled for S-mode and G-stage address translation when the Svadu extension is implemented.
RULE 27: When ADUE=1 in menvcfg, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 28: When the hypervisor extension is implemented and ADUE=1 in menvcfg, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during G-stage address translation, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for G-stage address translation.
RULE 29: When ADUE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though Svade is implemented for S-mode and G-stage address translation.
RULE 30: If Svadu is not implemented, the ADUE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 31: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero.
RULE 32: After changing menvcfg.ADUE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' A/D bits.
RULE 33: When ADUE=0 in menvcfg, Svade is implemented, requiring page-fault exceptions to be raised when PTE A/D bits need to be set.
RULE 34: When CDE=1 in menvcfg, the Smcdeleg extension is enabled.
RULE 35: When CDE=0 in menvcfg, the Smcdeleg and Ssccfg extensions appear to be not implemented.
RULE 36: If the Smcdeleg extension is not implemented, the CDE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 37: When the Sstc extension is not implemented, the STCE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 38: The STCE bit in menvcfg enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one.
RULE 39: When the Sstc extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt to access stimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception, henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero, and STIP in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if the extension were not implemented.
RULE 40: If the H extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, hip.VSTIP also reverts its defined behavior as if the extension were not implemented.
RULE 41: When the Zicboz extension is not implemented, the CBZE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 42: When CBZE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block zero instruction CBO.ZERO in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 43: When CBZE is not set to one in menvcfg, the CBO.ZERO instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 44: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBCFE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 45: When CBCFE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block clean instruction CBO.CLEAN and the cache block flush instruction CBO.FLUSH in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 46: When CBCFE is not set to one in menvcfg, CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH raise illegal-instruction exceptions in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 47: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, the CBIE field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 48: When CBIE=00b in menvcfg, the instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 49: Encoding 10b of the CBIE field in menvcfg is reserved.
RULE 50: When CBIE=01b in menvcfg and the instruction is enabled for execution in modes less privileged than M, the instruction is executed and performs a flush operation even if configured by a less privileged mode to perform a invalidate operation.
RULE 51: When CBIE=11b in menvcfg and the instruction is enabled for execution in modes less privileged than M, the instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation unless configured by a less privileged mode to perform a flush operation.
RULE 52: The CBIE field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 53: When the Smnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 54: The PMM field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 55: The PMM field in menvcfg enables or disables pointer masking for the next-lower privilege mode according to Table 19.
RULE 56: When LPE=1 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in S-mode.
RULE 57: When LPE=1 in menvcfg and S-mode is not implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in U-mode.
RULE 58: When LPE=0 in menvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in S-mode.
RULE 59: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the hart does not update the ELP state, which remains NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 60: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.
RULE 61: When LPE=0 in menvcfg and S-mode is not implemented, the hart does not update the ELP state (remaining NO_LP_EXPECTED) and the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op in U-mode.
RULE 62: When SSE=1 in menvcfg, the Zicfiss extension is activated in S-mode.
RULE 63: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to the behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 64: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the pte.xwr=010b encoding in VS/S-stage page tables becomes reserved.
RULE 65: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 66: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE fields are read-only zero.
RULE 67: When DTE=0 in menvcfg, the implementation behaves as though the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented.
RULE 68: When XLEN=64, the menvcfgh register does not exist, providing no alias for menvcfg.
RULE 69: If U-mode is not supported, the menvcfg register does not exist.
RULE 70: If U-mode is not supported, the menvcfgh register does not exist, providing no alias for menvcfg.
RULE 71: If the current privilege mode is M or S and siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, then any attempt to access a sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception when menvcfg.CDE is 0.
RULE 72: If the current privilege mode is VS, vsiselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and menvcfg.CDE is 0, then any attempt to access a vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 73: If the current privilege mode is VS, vsiselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and menvcfg.CDE is 1, then any attempt to access a vsireg* raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 74: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to access scountinhibit raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 75: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, if menvcfg.CDE = 1 then an attempt to read scountovf from VS-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 76: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, if menvcfg.CDE = 1 then an attempt to read scountovf from VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 77: When menvcfg.SSE is 1, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.
RULE 78: When menvcfg.SSE is 1, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises a virtual-instruction exception in VU-mode.
RULE 79: If the Svadu extension is implemented, the menvcfg.ADUE field is writable.
RULE 80: If menvcfg.SSE is 1, executing SSAMOSWAP.W or SSAMOSWAP.D must raise a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 81: When the PBMTE or ADUE bits in menvcfg are changed, an HFENCE.GVMA instruction with rs1 = x0 and rs2 = x0 suffices to synchronize with respect to the altered interpretation of G-stage and VS-stage PTEs' PBMT and A/D bit fields, respectively.
RULE 82: If S-mode is implemented and the current privilege mode is S or HS, the LPE field in the menvcfg register supplies the xLPE state.
RULE 83: If S-mode is not implemented and the current privilege mode is U, the LPE field in the menvcfg register supplies the xLPE state.
RULE 84: Attempts to access the ssp CSR may raise either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception depending on the value of the menvcfg.SSE field (as well as the senvcfg.SSE and henvcfg.SSE fields).
RULE 85: If the current privilege mode is less than M and the menvcfg.SSE field is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised when accessing the ssp CSR.
RULE 86: In S-mode and HS-mode, the architectural xSSE setting is determined by the value of the menvcfg.SSE field.
RULE 87: In M-mode, the architectural xSSE setting is always 0 regardless of the value of the menvcfg.SSE field.
RULE 88: Updates to the menvcfg.SSE field that affect xSSE take effect immediately and do not require address-translation caches to be synchronized with SFENCE.VMA, HFENCE.GVMA, or HFENCE.VVMA instructions.
RULE 89: When menvcfg.SSE=0, the encoding R=0, W=1, X=0 remains reserved.

REGISTER: mepc
NUMBER: 0x341
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: Smdbltrp, Smrnmi
RULE 1: The mepc CSR resides at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mepc CSR has machine read/write (MRW) access permissions.
RULE 3: When the Smrnmi extension is implemented and mnstatus.NMIE = 1, an unexpected trap causes the mnepc register to be written with the same value that the trap would have written to the mepc register.
RULE 4: When a trap is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg so that the trap occurs in S-mode instead of M-mode, the mepc register is not written.
RULE 5: mepc is an MXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 6: The least-significant bit of mepc (mepc[0]) is always zero.
RULE 7: On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, both low bits of mepc (mepc[1] and mepc[0]) are always zero.
RULE 8: If an implementation permits IALIGN to be either 16 or 32, then when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] is masked on reads so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 9: The read masking of mepc[1] when IALIGN=32 also applies to the implicit read performed by the MRET instruction.
RULE 10: Although masked on reads when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] remains writable.
RULE 11: mepc is a WARL register that MUST be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 12: When address translation is not in effect, the set of addresses that mepc must be able to represent includes all physical addresses that can be used as a valid program counter or effective address.
RULE 13: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that caused the exception.
RULE 14: In all other circumstances, mepc is never written by the implementation, although software may explicitly write mepc.
RULE 15: For a breakpoint exception raised by C.EBREAK, the virtual address of the faulting instruction is already recorded in mepc.
RULE 16: When an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, mepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 17: On an illegal-instruction exception, mepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 18: When a non-maskable interrupt (NMI) occurs, the mepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted.
RULE 19: When a non-maskable interrupt (UNMI) occurs, the hardware overwrites the current mepc register with the address of the NMI handler executing in machine mode.
RULE 20: If the hart was executing machine-mode code in a trap handler when a UNMI occurs, the previous value of mepc cannot be recovered.
RULE 21: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the CSR mepc.
RULE 22: The write to mepc occurs only when a trap is taken into M-mode (i.e., the trap is not delegated to a lower privilege mode).
RULE 23: mepc is written as part of the set of CSRs that are updated on trap entry.
RULE 24: During execution of the MRET instruction, the hardware sets the program counter (pc) to the value contained in the mepc register.

REGISTER: mhartid
NUMBER: 0xf14
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ID
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mhartid CSR is defined to be accessed only at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mhartid CSR has machine read-only (MRO) access, meaning it can be read but not written by software.
RULE 3: The mhartid CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register that contains the integer ID of the hardware thread executing the code.
RULE 4: The mhartid register MUST be readable in any implementation.
RULE 5: One hart MUST have a hart ID of zero as read from mhartid.
RULE 6: Hart IDs read from mhartid MUST be unique within the execution environment.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter10
NUMBER: 0xb0a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter10 has MRW access, meaning it is a machine-privileged read/write register.
RULE 2: A conforming implementation may implement mhpmcounter10 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 3: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter10 contains an arbitrary (implementation-dependent) value.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter10 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: The value programmed in the 64-bit WARL register mhpmevent10 directly determines which events cause mhpmcounter10 to increment.
RULE 6: When XLEN=64, a read of mhpmcounter10 accesses the full 64-bit value.
RULE 7: When XLEN=64, a write to mhpmcounter10 updates the full 64-bit value.
RULE 8: The HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register controls the accessibility of the mhpmcounter10 register to lower privilege modes.
RULE 9: If the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the mhpmcounter10 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter10 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 11: The hpmcounter10 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter10 hardware counter.
RULE 12: The mhpmcounter10 hardware counter continues to increment regardless of the state of the HPM10 bit in the mcounteren register.
RULE 13: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the mhpmcounter10 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 14: When the HPM10 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter10 increments as usual.
RULE 15: When the HPM10 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter10 does not increment.
RULE 16: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, treating the HPM10 bit as clear and causing mhpmcounter10 to increment as usual.
RULE 17: The OF bit in the mhpmevent10 register is set when mhpmcounter10 overflows and remains set until software writes the OF bit.
RULE 18: An overflow of mhpmcounter10 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, causing the counter to wrap around while the sticky OF bit stays set.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter10 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter10 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: The OF bit associated with mhpmcounter10 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 22: Count overflow of mhpmcounter10 never results from writes to mhpmcounter10 or mhpmevent10, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 23: If an INH bit for privilege mode x in mhpmevent10 is set, counting of events by mhpmcounter10 in privilege mode x is inhibited.
RULE 24: If privilege mode x is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent10 reads as zero.
RULE 25: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent10 are zero, mhpmcounter10 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 26: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit for mhpmevent10, reflecting the overflow status of mhpmcounter10.
RULE 27: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter10 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 28: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter10 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 29: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip serves as the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter10, and the corresponding LCOFIE bit in mie/sie serves as the interrupt-enable bit.
RULE 30: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter10 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 31: There are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmcounter10; the OF bit serves both purposes.
RULE 32: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter10 is performed by clearing its OF bit while initializing mhpmcounter10 to a starting value.
RULE 33: After mhpmcounter10 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter10 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter11
NUMBER: 0xb0b
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter11 is a machine-level CSR that is readable and writable (MRW).
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter11 contains an arbitrary (undefined) value.
RULE 3: Writing a value to mhpmcounter11 updates the register after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: The event selector CSR for mhpmcounter11 is mhpmevent11, which is a 64-bit WARL register.
RULE 5: Event 0 selected in mhpmevent11 (the selector for mhpmcounter11) is defined to mean no event, so mhpmcounter11 does not increment.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter11 and its corresponding event selector mhpmevent11 read-only zero.
RULE 7: The high-half event selector CSR mhpmevent11h for mhpmcounter11 is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 8: The mhpmcounter11 hardware performance-monitoring counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 9: The CSR hpmcounter11 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter11.
RULE 10: If the HPM11 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM11 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 12: In a hart that implements U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its HPM11 field is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that reads of the mhpmcounter11 shadow hpmcounter11 from less-privileged modes will raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: The OF bit in the corresponding mhpmevent11 register is set to 1 when mhpmcounter11 overflows and remains 1 until software writes it to 0.
RULE 14: Overflow of mhpmcounter11 is defined as an unsigned increment that wraps the implemented counter bits from their maximum value to zero.
RULE 15: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, the counter continues counting by wrapping around.
RULE 16: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, the OF bit remains set, preserving the overflow indication.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If mhpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent11 disables further count-overflow interrupt requests from mhpmcounter11.
RULE 20: When mhpmcounter11 overflows and generates an interrupt, bit 13 (LCOFIP) in the appropriate local-interrupt pending register (mip for M-mode, sip for S-mode) is set.
RULE 21: After mhpmcounter11's OF bit becomes one, the LCOFIP bit will later be set, and software must clear LCOFIP before servicing the overflow interrupt.
RULE 22: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter11 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the appropriate bit(s) in the mideleg register.
RULE 23: Writing to mhpmcounter11 cannot cause an overflow; only hardware-performed increments can cause overflow.
RULE 24: If supervisor mode is implemented, bit 11 of the scountovf register provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter11.
RULE 25: If MINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 26: If SINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 27: If UINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 28: If VSINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 29: If VUINH in mhpmevent11 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter11 is inhibited while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 30: For each INH bit, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the INH bit in mhpmevent11 reads as zero and cannot inhibit counting for mhpmcounter11.
RULE 31: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, software must write a new starting value to mhpmcounter11 before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 32: After mhpmcounter11 overflows, software must clear the OF bit before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter12
NUMBER: 0xb0c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter12 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter12 may be written with a given value.
RULE 3: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter12 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: If the high-half CSR mhpmcounter12h is implemented, reads of mhpmcounter12h return bits 63-32 of mhpmcounter12 and writes to mhpmcounter12h modify only bits 63-32 of mhpmcounter12.
RULE 5: If mhpmevent12 is set to 0, mhpmcounter12 is not incremented by any event.
RULE 6: A legal implementation MAY make mhpmcounter12 read-only 0 together with its corresponding event selector mhpmevent12.
RULE 7: The mhpmcounter12 register continues to increment even when it is not accessible, and reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter12 counter.
RULE 8: The hpmcountern12 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter12 register.
RULE 9: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the mhpmcounter12 value via its hpmcountern12 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter12 value via its hpmcountern12 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: When the HPM12 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter12 register increments as usual.
RULE 12: When the HPM12 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter12 register does not increment.
RULE 13: The settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only whether the mhpmcounter12 register increments and do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter12 register.
RULE 14: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, so the HPM12 bit is effectively clear and the mhpmcounter12 register increments as usual.
RULE 15: The OF bit in the mhpmevent register that is associated with mhpmcounter12 is set when mhpmcounter12 overflows, and remains set until written by software.
RULE 16: Overflow of mhpmcounter12 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter12 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter12 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: The OF bit associated with mhpmcounter12 functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for that counter.
RULE 20: Count overflow of mhpmcounter12 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter12 or its mhpmevent12 register; it occurs only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 21: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter12 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 22: When the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter12 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 23: The LCOFIP bit in mip and sip and the LCOFIE bit in mie and sie are, respectively, the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter12.
RULE 24: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter12 corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 25: The mideleg register controls delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter12 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 26: For mhpmcounter12 there are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits; the OF bit serves both functions.
RULE 27: Overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter12 is enabled by clearing its OF bit, which must be done together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 28: After mhpmcounter12 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 29: If a privilege mode x associated with an INH bit for mhpmcounter12 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 30: Each of the five x INH bits for mhpmcounter12, when set, inhibits counting of events while in privilege mode x; if all five bits are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 31: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter12.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter13
NUMBER: 0xb0d
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter13 has privilege MRW, meaning it is a machine-mode read/write CSR and is readable and writable only in machine mode.
RULE 2: mhpmcounter13 is a WARL register.
RULE 3: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter13 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 4: mhpmcounter13 can be written with a given value.
RULE 5: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter13 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The event selector CSR mhpmevent13 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter13 to increment.
RULE 7: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event" for the selector that controls mhpmcounter13.
RULE 8: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter13 be read-only 0.
RULE 9: The hpmcounter13 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter13.
RULE 10: Access to the read-only shadow CSR hpmcounter13 of mhpmcounter13 is permitted only when the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set; if the HPM13 bit is clear, a read of hpmcounter13 from S-mode or U-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: When the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set, a read of hpmcounter13 (the shadow of mhpmcounter13) is permitted in the next implemented lower privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 12: The settings in the mcounteren register do not affect the counting operation of mhpmcounter13; mhpmcounter13 continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 13: If the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter13 register increments as usual.
RULE 14: If the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter13 register does not increment.
RULE 15: The settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only the incrementing behavior of the mhpmcounter13 register and do not affect its accessibility.
RULE 16: When the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, causing the mhpmcounter13 register to increment as usual.
RULE 17: When the siselect CSR holds a value that selects counter 13, the CSR sireg (or sireg2) could be used to access the mhpmcounter13 register.
RULE 18: Each x INH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events in mhpmcounter13 while executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 19: When all INH bits in mhpmevent13 are zero, mhpmcounter13 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 20: The OF bit in mhpmevent13 is set when mhpmcounter13 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 21: Overflow of mhpmcounter13 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 22: After an overflow, mhpmcounter13 wraps around and continues counting while its OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 23: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register bit 13 provides a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter13.
RULE 24: If mhpmcounter13 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: If mhpmcounter13 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: The OF bit associated with mhpmcounter13 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for that counter.
RULE 27: Count overflow for mhpmcounter13 never results from writes to mhpmcounter13 or mhpmevent13; it only results from hardware increments of mhpmcounter13.
RULE 28: A count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter13 is signaled as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 29: The mip/sip LCOFIP bit 13 is the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter13.
RULE 30: The mie/sie LCOFIE bit 13 is the interrupt-enable bit for the overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter13.
RULE 31: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by mhpmcounter13 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 32: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter13 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit 13 in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 33: The mideleg register controls delegation of the overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter13 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 34: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter13 is done by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 35: Once mhpmcounter13 has overflowed, it and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter14
NUMBER: 0xb0e
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter14 is a Machine-level Read/Write CSR.
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter14 contains an arbitrary value until software writes a value to it.
RULE 3: A write to the mhpmcounter14 CSR takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: The 64-bit WARL event selector CSR mhpmevent14 determines which hardware event causes mhpmcounter14 to increment.
RULE 5: Event code 0 selected in mhpmevent14 is defined to mean that no event increments mhpmcounter14.
RULE 6: Implementations SHOULD provide mhpmcounter14, but a legal implementation may make mhpmcounter14 read-only and fixed to zero.
RULE 7: The lower XLEN bits of mhpmcounter14 are accessed through the hpmcounter14 CSR, which is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter14.
RULE 8: The mhpmcounter14 register continues to increment even when it is not accessible from lower privilege modes.
RULE 9: If the HPM14 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of mhpmcounter14 from S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM14 bit in the mcounteren register is set, a read of mhpmcounter14 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: In harts that implement U-mode, the HPM14 field of the mcounteren register is a WARL field that may be read-only zero, and when it is zero a read of mhpmcounter14 from a less-privileged mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: In harts without U-mode, the mcounteren register is read-only and its HPM14 field may be read-only zero, causing reads of mhpmcounter14 from a less-privileged mode to cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the HPM14 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter14 register increments as usual.
RULE 14: If the HPM14 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter14 register does not increment.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, making the HPM14 bit effectively clear and causing the mhpmcounter14 register to increment as usual.
RULE 16: The OF bit in mhpmevent14 is set when mhpmcounter14 overflows, and remains set until written by software.
RULE 17: Overflow of mhpmcounter14 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, causing the counter to wrap around and continue counting while the OF bit remains set.
RULE 18: When supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmcounter14.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter14 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: Writes to mhpmcounter14 or mhpmevent14 never cause count overflow; overflow occurs only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter14.
RULE 21: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by mhpmcounter14, its OF bit is set.
RULE 22: After the OF bit for mhpmcounter14 becomes set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers is eventually set, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 23: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter14 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 24: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent14 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero for mhpmcounter14.
RULE 25: Setting any of the MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH bits in mhpmevent14 inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter14 while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 26: After mhpmcounter14 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter15
NUMBER: 0xb0f
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter15 is a WARL register.
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter15 holds an arbitrary value.
RULE 3: A write to mhpmcounter15 becomes visible only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: If mhpmevent15 is programmed with the value 0, mhpmcounter15 will not increment for any event.
RULE 5: A legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter15 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 6: mhpmevent15h exists only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, and its presence can affect which events increment mhpmcounter15.
RULE 7: mhpmcounter15 increments according to the event selected in mhpmevent15, and additionally according to the event selected in mhpmevent15h when that CSR exists.
RULE 8: The CSR hpmcounter15 is a read-only shadow of the hardware performance-monitoring counter mhpmcounter15.
RULE 9: When the HPM 15 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the mhpmcounter15 shadow CSR hpmcounter15 while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the HPM 15 bit in mcounteren is set, access to the mhpmcounter15 shadow CSR hpmcounter15 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: The settings of the HPM 15 bit in mcounteren do not affect the mhpmcounter15 counter, which continues to increment even when the mhpmcounter15 shadow CSR is not accessible.
RULE 12: The mhpmcounter15 register increments as usual when the HPM15 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear.
RULE 13: The mhpmcounter15 register does not increment when the HPM15 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set.
RULE 14: The accessibility of the mhpmcounter15 register is not affected by the settings of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 15: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, causing the HPM15 bit to be considered clear and the mhpmcounter15 register to increment as usual.
RULE 16: The OF field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 17: The MINH field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 inhibits counting of events in M-mode when set.
RULE 18: The SINH field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 19: The UINH field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 inhibits counting of events in U-mode when set.
RULE 20: The VSINH field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 inhibits counting of events in VS-mode when set.
RULE 21: The VUINH field in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 inhibits counting of events in VU-mode when set.
RULE 22: The WPRI fields in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 are reserved.
RULE 23: For each INH bit associated with mhpmcounter15, if the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 24: When an INH bit for mhpmcounter15 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is executing in the associated privilege mode.
RULE 25: If all INH bits for mhpmcounter15 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 26: The OF bit in the mhpmevent15 register associated with mhpmcounter15 is set when the corresponding mhpmcounter15 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 27: Overflow for mhpmcounter15 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 28: No loss of information occurs after an overflow of mhpmcounter15 because the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 29: If mhpmcounter15 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 30: If the OF bit for mhpmcounter15 is one, then no interrupt request is generated, and the OF bit also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter15.
RULE 31: Count overflow for mhpmcounter15 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter15 or its associated mhpmevent15 registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 32: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter15 corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, with the LCOFIP and LCOFIE bits serving as the pending and enable bits respectively.
RULE 33: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter15 sets its OF bit.
RULE 34: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter15 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 35: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter15 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 36: Once mhpmcounter15 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 37: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter15 is done by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter16
NUMBER: 0xb10
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter16 contains an arbitrary value, and it can be written with a specified value.
RULE 2: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter16 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: All counters should be implemented, but a legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter16 as a read-only zero register together with its event selector mhpmevent16.
RULE 4: If mhpmevent16 is programmed with the value 0, which denotes "no event," then mhpmcounter16 does not increment for any event.
RULE 5: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of mhpmcounter16 in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter16 is permitted in S-mode when S-mode is implemented, otherwise it is permitted in U-mode.
RULE 7: The hpmcounter16 CSR is a read-only shadow of the underlying mhpmcounter16 register.
RULE 8: The value of mhpmcounter16 continues to increment regardless of whether the HPM16 bit in mcounteren is clear or set, and accesses to mcounteren do not affect its count.
RULE 9: When the HPM16 field of mcounteren is a read-only zero WARL value, a read of mhpmcounter16 in a less-privileged mode (S-mode or U-mode) causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 63 named OF, which is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 62 named MINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in M-mode.
RULE 12: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 61 named SINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in S/HS-mode.
RULE 13: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 60 named UINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in U-mode.
RULE 14: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 59 named VSINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in VS-mode.
RULE 15: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 58 named VUINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in VU-mode.
RULE 16: For each INH bit in mhpmevent16, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit reads as zero for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 17: All INH bits cleared to zero in mhpmevent16 result in mhpmcounter16 counting events in all modes.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 19: Overflow of mhpmcounter16 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter16 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 21: When supervisor mode is implemented, scountovf bit 16 is a read-only shadow copy of mhpmevent16.OF for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter16 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: If mhpmcounter16's OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated for that overflow.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 25: Writes to mhpmcounter16 never cause a count overflow; overflow only results from hardware increments of mhpmcounter16.
RULE 26: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter16 is mapped to local interrupt bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 27: The mip (or sip) LCOFIP bit is the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 28: The mie (or sie) LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 29: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter16 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent16.
RULE 30: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter16 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 31: Software clears the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from mhpmcounter16.
RULE 32: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 33: After mhpmcounter16 has overflowed, software must write a new value to mhpmcounter16 and clear mhpmevent16.OF before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

RULE 1: mhpmcounter17 is a machine-level CSR that provides read/write (MRW) privilege.

RULE 10: When the HPM17 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter17 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).

RULE 19: Overflow of mhpmcounter17 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter17 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 21: If mhpmcounter17 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter17 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: The OF bit for mhpmcounter17 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter17.

RULE 32: If the SINH bit (bit 61 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 33: If the UINH bit (bit 60 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in U-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 34: If the VSINH bit (bit 59 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in VS-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 35: If the VUINH bit (bit 58 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in VU-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.

RULE 31: For each INH bit in mhpmevent5, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero for mhpmcounter5.
