RULE 33: After mhpmcounter5 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter6
NUMBER: 0xb06
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: Event 0 selected in mhpmevent6 is defined to mean that no event increments mhpmcounter6.
RULE 2: A legal implementation may make mhpmcounter6 read-only zero.
RULE 3: When the HPM6 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter6 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception, and this restriction applies to accesses that would otherwise read the mhpmcounter6 register.
RULE 4: The hpmcounter6 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter6 register.
RULE 5: The mhpmcounter6 register continues to increment even when the HPM6 bit in the mcounteren register is cleared.
RULE 6: The settings in the mcountinhibit register control whether mhpmcounter6 increments, and they do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter6.
RULE 7: When the HPM 6 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 8: When the HPM 6 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter6 does not increment.
RULE 9: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the HPM 6 bit were clear, so mhpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 10: When mhpmcounter6 overflows, the OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set and remains set until written by software.
RULE 11: Overflow of mhpmcounter6 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits because mhpmcounter6 values are unsigned.
RULE 12: After mhpmcounter6 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent6 remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 13: For each privilege mode x, if the privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in mhpmevent6 for mhpmcounter6 is read-only zero.
RULE 14: When an x INH bit in mhpmevent6 for mhpmcounter6 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter6 is inhibited while executing in privilege mode x, and when all x INH bits are zero, mhpmcounter6 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 15: Writes to mhpmcounter6 or mhpmevent6 never cause a count overflow; count overflow for mhpmcounter6 occurs only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 16: If mhpmcounter6 overflows while its associated OF bit in mhpmevent6 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 17: If the OF bit associated with mhpmcounter6 in mhpmevent6 is one, a count overflow interrupt request is not generated.
RULE 18: A count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 19: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6.
RULE 20: The LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6.
RULE 21: When mhpmcounter6 generates a count-overflow-interrupt request, its OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set.
RULE 22: After the OF bit for mhpmcounter6 in mhpmevent6 is set, the corresponding LCOFIP bit in mip or sip will eventually be set.
RULE 23: The LCOFIP bit for mhpmcounter6 is cleared by software before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from one or more overflows of mhpmcounter6.
RULE 24: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by mhpmcounter6 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter7
NUMBER: 0xb07
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter7 is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 2: mhpmcounter7h is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 3: mhpmcounter7 is one of the hardware-performance monitor's additional 64-bit event counters (mhpmcounter3–mhpmcounter31) and is a 64-bit counter.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter7 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter7 may be written with any value.
RULE 6: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter7 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: mhpmevent7 is a 64-bit WARL register whose programmed value determines which event causes mhpmcounter7 to increment.
RULE 8: If mhpmevent7 = 0, mhpmcounter7 does not increment for any event.
RULE 9: A legal implementation may choose to make mhpmcounter7 read-only zero, in which case reads of mhpmcounter7 return 0 and writes have no effect.
RULE 10: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is set, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) is permitted in the next lower implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 12: The settings in mcounteren affect only accessibility and do not affect mhpmcounter7, which continues to increment regardless of the HPM7 bit state.
RULE 13: The increment behavior of mhpmcounter7 is controlled by the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 14: The settings of the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter7.
RULE 15: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter7 increments as usual.
RULE 16: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter7 does not increment.
RULE 17: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as though the register were set to zero, making the HPM7 bit effectively clear and causing mhpmcounter7 to increment as usual.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent7 is set when mhpmcounter7 overflows and remains set until software writes to it.
RULE 19: An overflow of mhpmcounter7 occurs when its unsigned value wraps past the most-significant implemented counter bit.
RULE 20: After mhpmcounter7 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while its OF bit stays set.
RULE 21: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent7 disables further count-overflow interrupt requests for mhpmcounter7.
RULE 24: mhpmcounter7 can overflow only as a result of hardware increments and never as a result of software writes to mhpmcounter7 or mhpmevent7.
RULE 25: An overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter7 sets the LCOFIP pending bit (bit 13) in mip and sip, and the corresponding LCOFIE enable bits in mie and sie control whether the interrupt is enabled.
RULE 26: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt by mhpmcounter7 sets its OF bit and eventually sets the LCOFIP pending bit in mip and sip.
RULE 27: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter7 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 28: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmcounter7; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing the counter.
RULE 29: After mhpmcounter7 has overflowed, both the counter value and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 30: Setting any INH bit in mhpmevent7 (e.g., MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter7 while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if that privilege mode is not implemented the INH bit reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter8
NUMBER: 0xb08
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The CSR mhpmevent8 selects the event counted by mhpmcounter8.
RULE 2: The event that causes mhpmcounter8 to increment is selected by the corresponding event-selector CSR mhpmevent8.
RULE 3: If a legal implementation chooses to make the counter and its event selector read-only 0, then mhpmcounter8 reads as zero and cannot be written.
RULE 4: When XLEN = 64, reads of mhpmcounter8 access the full 64-bit register value.
RULE 5: When XLEN = 64, writes of mhpmcounter8 access the full 64-bit register value.
RULE 6: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the hpmcounter8 CSR (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter8) while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter8 CSR (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter8) is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 8: The hpmcounter8 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter8 register.
RULE 9: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter8 register increments as usual.
RULE 10: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter8 register does not increment.
RULE 11: The setting of the mcountinhibit register does not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter8 register.
RULE 12: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the mhpmcounter8 register increments as if the HPM 8 bit were clear.
RULE 13: When the siselect value selects counter 8, the sireg and sireg2 registers can be used to access the mhpmcounter8 register and the corresponding mhpmevent8 register.
RULE 14: When the siselect value selects counter 8, the sireg4 and sireg5 registers can be used to access the high-half register mhpmcounter8h (the high half of mhpmcounter8) and the corresponding mhpmevent8h register.
RULE 15: Bit 63 of the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is named OF and functions as an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the mhpmcounter8 overflows.
RULE 16: When the OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter8 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If the OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: The OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for mhpmcounter8.
RULE 20: The OF bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is set when mhpmcounter8 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 21: Overflow of mhpmcounter8 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of mhpmcounter8.
RULE 22: After mhpmcounter8 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 23: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter8 sets its OF bit.
RULE 24: The LCOFIP bits in the mip and sip registers are the interrupt-pending bits and the LCOFIE bits in the mie and sie registers are the interrupt-enable bits for the mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt.
RULE 25: The mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt request is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 26: The mideleg register controls delegation of the mhpmcounter8 overflow interrupt to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 27: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter8 is done by clearing the OF bit together with initializing mhpmcounter8 to a starting value.
RULE 28: After mhpmcounter8 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter8 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 29: Count overflow of mhpmcounter8 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter8 or its mhpmevent8 register, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter8.
RULE 30: Each of the five x INH bits in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 31: If all five x INH bits in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 32: If a privilege mode x is not implemented, the corresponding x INH bit in the mhpmcounter8 mhpmevent register is read-only zero.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter9
NUMBER: 0xb09
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter9 is a Machine-level CSR that is readable and writable by machine mode (privilege MRW).
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter9 contains an arbitrary value.
RULE 3: After a hart reset, software may write an arbitrary value into mhpmcounter9.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter9 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: The event-selector CSR mhpmevent9 is a 64-bit WARL register that determines which event causes mhpmcounter9 to increment.
RULE 6: Event value 0 selected in mhpmevent9 is defined to mean "no event" for mhpmcounter9.
RULE 7: Implementations SHOULD provide mhpmcounter9, but a legal implementation may instead make mhpmcounter9 read-only zero.
RULE 8: The CSR mhpmcounter9h exists only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented; otherwise only the low-half CSR mhpmcounter9 is present.
RULE 9: The CSR mhpmcounter9h provides access to bits 63-32 of mhpmcounter9 when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 10: The CSR mhpmevent9h is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and forms part of the 64-bit event selector value for mhpmcounter9.
RULE 11: mhpmcounter9 is a hardware performance-monitoring counter whose value can be observed through its read-only shadow CSR.
RULE 12: The CSR hpmcounter9 provides a read-only view of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 13: If the HPM9 bit in mcounteren is clear, an attempt to read the shadow CSR hpmcounter9 while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception, thereby denying access to mhpmcounter9.
RULE 14: If the HPM9 bit in mcounteren is set, access to the shadow CSR hpmcounter9 is permitted in the next lower implemented privilege mode, allowing observation of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 15: Reading or writing the shadow CSR hpmcounter9 does not affect mhpmcounter9, which continues to increment independently.
RULE 16: mhpmcounter9 continues to increment even when its shadow CSR is inaccessible due to the HPM9 bit being clear.
RULE 17: The accessibility of mhpmcounter9 is not affected by the mcountinhibit CSR.
RULE 18: When the HPM 9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter9 increments as usual.
RULE 19: When the HPM 9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter9 does not increment.
RULE 20: If the mcountinhibit register is not implemented, the implementation behaves as if the register were zero, treating the HPM 9 bit as clear and causing mhpmcounter9 to increment as usual.
RULE 21: When the siselect value selects counter 9, the mhpmcounter9 register (and its associated mhpmevent9) may be accessed through the sireg or sireg2 registers.
RULE 22: When the siselect value selects counter 9, the mhpmcounter9h register (and its associated mhpmevent9h) may be accessed through the sireg4 or sireg5 registers.
RULE 23: Implementations are expected (non-normative) to raise an illegal-instruction exception for an indirect access to mhpmcounter9 via mireg* when miselect contains an unimplemented value.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 is set when mhpmcounter9 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 25: Overflow of mhpmcounter9 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 26: After an overflow, mhpmcounter9 wraps around and continues counting while its sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 27: Each xINH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode for mhpmcounter9.
RULE 28: If all five xINH bits in mhpmevent9 are zero, mhpmcounter9 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: If a privilege mode associated with an xINH bit is not implemented, that xINH bit reads as zero for mhpmcounter9.
RULE 30: If mhpmcounter9 overflows while its OF bit in mhpmevent9 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 31: If the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is one when mhpmcounter9 overflows, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter9.
RULE 33: Count overflow of mhpmcounter9 never results from writes to mhpmcounter9 or mhpmevent9 registers; it occurs only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal generated by mhpmcounter9 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 35: The mip/sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits and the mie/sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter9.
RULE 36: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter9 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent9.
RULE 37: When the OF bit in mhpmevent9 for mhpmcounter9 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 38: Software clears the LCOFIP bit before servicing the count-overflow interrupt resulting from one or more overflows of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter9 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 40: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter9 is performed by clearing its OF bit together with initializing mhpmcounter9 to a starting value.
RULE 41: After mhpmcounter9 has overflowed, both mhpmcounter9 and its OF bit must be re-initialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 42: The OF field in mhpmevent9 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when mhpmcounter9 overflows.

REGISTER: mhpmevent10
NUMBER: 0x32a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmevent10 belongs to the Machine Counter Setup group and has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the mhpmevent10.OF bit is set and the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the mhpmevent10.OF bit does not cause the LCOFIP bit in the mip register to become set, and the LCOFIP bit remains zero.
RULE 4: An event value of 0 programmed in mhpmevent10 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 5: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent10 read-only 0.
RULE 6: The CSR mhpmevent10h, which provides the high half of mhpmevent10, is present only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 7: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent10 is accessed through the indirect sireg* alias, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent10 is read-only 0.
RULE 8: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, and menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: When the privilege mode is M or S and siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg3 alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the privilege mode is M or S and siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg6 alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, XLEN = 64, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg4 alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, XLEN = 64, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg5 alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the privilege mode is M or S and siselect = 0x41, any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: When the privilege mode is M or S, siselect selects a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, and the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), any attempt to access mhpmevent10 via the sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If any extension on which the state accessed by mhpmevent10 depends is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent10 through the sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: If the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access mhpmevent10.
RULE 17: While the hypervisor extension is implemented and vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt from VS-mode to access mhpmevent10 via the vsireg* (sireg*) alias raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 18: While the hypervisor extension is implemented and vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt from VS-mode to access mhpmevent10 via the vsireg* (sireg*) alias raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 19: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 20: The MINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 21: The SINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 22: The UINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 23: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual supervisor mode.
RULE 24: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual user mode.
RULE 25: Bits 56 and 57 of mhpmevent10 are reserved (WPRI) and have no defined architectural function.
RULE 26: If a privilege mode associated with an x INH bit in mhpmevent10 is not implemented, that x INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 27: When an x INH bit in mhpmevent10 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited.
RULE 28: When all x INH bits in mhpmevent10 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 30: Overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent10 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 31: After an overflow, the counter associated with mhpmevent10 continues counting while the OF bit remains set, so no information is lost.
RULE 32: If the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is zero when its hpmcounter overflows, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: If the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is one when its hpmcounter overflows, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 34: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 35: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, including mhpmevent10; only hardware increments cause overflow.
RULE 36: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated for mhpmevent10 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 37: The LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers is the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10.
RULE 38: The LCOFIE bit in the mie/sie registers is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10.
RULE 39: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent10 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent10.
RULE 40: When the OF bit in mhpmevent10 becomes set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers.
RULE 41: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 42: There are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits in mhpmevent10.
RULE 43: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent10 is done by clearing the OF bit, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 44: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent10 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 45: The overflow (OF) bit in mhpmevent10 is mirrored as a shadow copy in scountovf bit 10.
RULE 46: Read access to the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is controlled by the same mcounteren (and, when applicable, hcounteren) bits that control access to hpmcounter10.
RULE 47: In M-mode, the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is always readable via its scountovf shadow.
RULE 48: In S-mode or HS-mode, the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is readable only when mcounteren bit 10 is set; otherwise a read returns zero.
RULE 49: In VS-mode, the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 10 and hcounteren bit 10 are set; otherwise a read returns zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent11
NUMBER: 0x32b
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the CSR mip.LCOFIP exists as an interrupt-pending bit that can be set when mhpmevent11.OF is set.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP is a read-write register.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from mhpmevent11.OF being set.
RULE 4: When mhpmevent11.OF is set and the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP will be set to indicate that a local-counter-overflow interrupt request has occurred.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, mip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero, so setting mhpmevent11.OF does not change mip.LCOFIP.
RULE 6: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, mie.LCOFIE is a read-only zero, so setting mhpmevent11.OF does not change mie.LCOFIE.
RULE 7: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting mhpmevent11.OF has no effect on any interrupt-pending or interrupt-enable bits.
RULE 8: mhpmevent11 is a 64-bit WARL CSR that selects the event which causes its associated performance counter to increment.
RULE 9: The platform defines the meaning of event codes written to mhpmevent11, and event code 0 is defined to indicate no event.
RULE 10: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent11 read-only and fixed to zero, and its associated counter also read-only zero.
RULE 11: A write to mhpmevent11 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 12: When the siselect register holds a value associated with counter 11, a read or write of sireg or sireg2 accesses the mhpmevent11 CSR, and a read or write of sireg4 or sireg5 accesses the mhpmevent11h CSR (the high-half of a 64-bit mhpmevent11, if implemented).
RULE 13: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, event selector bit 62 (named MINH) of mhpmevent11 is read-only and reads as 0 when the register is accessed through a sireg* alias.
RULE 14: When mhpmevent11 is accessed via the sireg* mechanism in M or S privilege mode with siselect in the range 0x40-0x5F, an illegal-instruction exception is raised if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 15: When mhpmevent11 is accessed via the sireg* mechanism in M or S privilege mode with siselect = 0x41, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 16: When mhpmevent11 is accessed via the sireg* mechanism in M or S privilege mode with siselect selecting a counter that is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 17: If any extension on which the underlying state of mhpmevent11 depends is not implemented, an attempt to access mhpmevent11 through sireg* in M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: The mhpmevent11.OF bit is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits that can generate a local counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 19: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent11.OF bit causes sip.LCOFIP to reflect that overflow interrupt request.
RULE 20: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero regardless of the mhpmevent11.OF bit.
RULE 21: Bits 63 through 56 of mhpmevent11 are defined as follows: bit 63 is OF, bit 62 is MINH, bit 61 is SINH, bit 60 is UINH, bit 59 is VSINH, bit 58 is VUINH, and bits 57 and 56 are WPRI.
RULE 22: For each INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent11, if the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.
RULE 23: Setting any of the INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent11 inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in the associated privilege mode.
RULE 24: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent11 are zero, event counting occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 25: The OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes a value to clear it.
RULE 26: Overflow for the purpose of setting the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 27: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: If the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: For mhpmevent11, count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers; it occurs only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 30: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the associated hpmcounter sets the OF bit in mhpmevent11.
RULE 31: When the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in mip and sip registers.
RULE 32: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent11 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 33: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent11 is performed by clearing its OF bit together with initializing the corresponding counter to a starting value.
RULE 34: After an overflow has occurred, both the counter associated with mhpmevent11 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 35: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent11 is shadowed in scountovf bit 11.
RULE 36: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent11 is always readable via scountovf bit 11.
RULE 37: In S-mode or HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent11 is readable via scountovf bit 11 only when mcounteren bit 11 is set, and reads as zero when mcounteren bit 11 is not set.
RULE 38: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent11 is readable via scountovf bit 11 only when both mcounteren bit 11 and hcounteren bit 11 are set, and reads as zero otherwise.
RULE 39: Reading scountovf bit 11 returns the current state of the OF bit of mhpmevent11, subject to the applicable access conditions.

REGISTER: mhpmevent12
NUMBER: 0x32c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent12 is accessed with Machine Read/Write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting mhpmevent12.OF to 1 can cause mip.LCOFIP to become set (pending).
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the state of mhpmevent12.OF has no effect on mip.LCOFIP.
RULE 4: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, mip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero regardless of the value of mhpmevent12.OF.
RULE 5: Writes to mhpmevent12 select the hardware event whose occurrences will cause mhpmcounter12 to increment.
RULE 6: Reads of mhpmevent12 return the currently selected event value.
RULE 7: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent12 selects "no event", causing mhpmcounter12 not to increment for any event.
RULE 8: When mhpmevent12 is read-only with a constant value 0, any write to mhpmevent12 has no effect and reads always return 0.
RULE 9: A write to mhpmevent12 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 10: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the CSR mhpmevent12h exists and provides access to bits 63-32 of mhpmevent12.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the CSR mhpmevent12h does not exist.
RULE 12: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent12 is accessed via sireg* (siselect = 0x4C), then bit 62 of mhpmevent12 MUST read as 0 and MUST be read-only (writes to that bit have no effect).
RULE 13: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, then any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent12 via sireg* (siselect = 0x4C) MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: If the counter selected by siselect = 0x4C is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren is 0), then any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent12 via sireg* MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If any extension upon which the mhpmevent12 counter state depends is not implemented, then any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent12 through sireg* MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: If any extension listed for the siselect = 0x4C entry that defines mhpmevent12 is not implemented, then any attempt from M-mode or S-mode to access mhpmevent12 via sireg* MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: Setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent12 causes the LCOFIP bit in the sip CSR to reflect the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 18: The LCOFIP bit in the sip CSR is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that results from the .OF bit of mhpmevent12 being set.
RULE 19: The OF field of mhpmevent12 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 20: The MINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in machine mode.
RULE 21: The SINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 22: The UINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in user mode.
RULE 23: The VSINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 24: The VUINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in virtual-user mode.
RULE 25: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit of mhpmevent12 is not implemented, the associated INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 26: When any INH bit of mhpmevent12 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited.
RULE 27: When all INH bits of mhpmevent12 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 28: The OF bit of mhpmevent12 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter experiences an unsigned overflow of its implemented bits and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: After the OF bit of mhpmevent12 becomes set, the associated hpmcounter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 30: A count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for mhpmevent12 when its associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent12 is zero.
RULE 31: No count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for mhpmevent12 when its associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent12 is one.
RULE 32: The OF bit of mhpmevent12 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 33: Overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent12 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal for mhpmevent12 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie CSRs.
RULE 35: The mip/sip LCOFIP bit and the mie/sie LCOFIE bit are, respectively, the pending and enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent12.
RULE 36: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent12 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent12.
RULE 37: When the OF bit of mhpmevent12 is set, it eventually causes the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip CSRs to become set.
RULE 38: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent12 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 39: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent12 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 40: The scountovf CSR bit 12 provides a shadow copy of the overflow (OF) bit from mhpmevent12.
RULE 41: In M-mode, the overflow flag of mhpmevent12 is always readable via scountovf bit 12.
RULE 42: In S-mode (or HS-mode), the overflow flag of mhpmevent12 is readable via scountovf bit 12 only when mcounteren bit 12 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 43: In VS-mode, the overflow flag of mhpmevent12 is readable via scountovf bit 12 only when both mcounteren bit 12 and hcounteren bit 12 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent13
NUMBER: 0x32d
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT

RULE 16: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent13 does not affect sip.LCOFIP because sip.LCOFIP is permanently a read-only zero.
RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent n .OF bit, including the .OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 18: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE bits are read-only zeros, so the .OF bit in mhpmevent13 cannot generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 19: The mhpmevent13 register bits 63-56 are defined as OF (bit 63), MINH (bit 62), SINH (bit 61), UINH (bit 60), VSINH (bit 59), VUINH (bit 58), and WPRI (bits 57-56, reserved).
RULE 20: The OF bit in mhpmevent13 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 21: The MINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 22: The SINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 23: The UINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 24: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 25: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.

RULE 27: If a privilege mode associated with an INH bit of mhpmevent13 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 28: When any INH bit of mhpmevent13 is set, it inhibits counting of events while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 29: When all INH bits of mhpmevent13 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 30: The OF bit in mhpmevent13 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 31: Since hpmcounter values are unsigned, overflow for the counter associated with mhpmevent13 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 32: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent13 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: If the OF bit of mhpmevent13 is one when its hpmcounter overflows, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 34: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent13 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 35: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent13.
RULE 36: The mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent13.
RULE 37: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent13 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 38: When the OF bit in mhpmevent13 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent13 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 40: Writing to mhpmevent13 never causes a count overflow; overflow can only result from hardware increments of the associated counter.
RULE 41: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for the counter linked to mhpmevent13; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 42: After the counter associated with mhpmevent13 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 43: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent13 is mirrored into bit 13 of the read-only CSR scountovf.

REGISTER: mhpmevent15

RULE 21: The two WPRI fields of bits 57 and 56 in mhpmevent15 are reserved.
RULE 22: The OF bit in mhpmevent15 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 23: The OF bit in mhpmevent15 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 24: If the supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent15.
RULE 25: If an hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent15 overflows while the OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: If the OF bit of mhpmevent15 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 27: Count overflow of the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent15 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 28: Count overflow for mhpmevent15 never results from software writes to mhpmevent15 or the corresponding mhpmcounter register, only from hardware increments.
RULE 29: The MINH bit of mhpmevent15, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 30: The SINH bit of mhpmevent15, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 31: The UINH bit of mhpmevent15, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 32: The VSINH bit of mhpmevent15, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 33: The VUINH bit of mhpmevent15, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 34: If any privilege mode associated with an INH bit of mhpmevent15 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 35: All INH bits of mhpmevent15 cleared to zero permit counting of events in all implemented privilege modes.
RULE 36: When a count overflow interrupt request is generated for the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent15, the corresponding LCOFIP bit (bit 13) in the mip and sip registers is eventually set.
RULE 37: The LCOFIE bits in the mie and sie registers enable the count overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent15.
RULE 38: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent15 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent15.
RULE 39: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent15 is performed by clearing the OF bit while initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 40: After the counter associated with mhpmevent15 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 41: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent15 is mirrored in scountovf bit 15.
RULE 42: In M-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent15 (as reflected by scountovf bit 15) is always readable.
RULE 43: In S-mode or HS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent15 (as reflected by scountovf bit 15) is readable only when mcounteren bit 15 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 44: In VS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent15 (as reflected by scountovf bit 15) is readable only when both mcounteren bit 15 and hcounteren bit 15 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent16
NUMBER: 0x330
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent16 causes the mip.LCOFIP bit to reflect the corresponding local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 2: mhpmevent16 is a 64-bit WARL CSR.
RULE 3: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent16 selects "no event" for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 4: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent16 is read-only 0 when accessed through a sireg* register.
RULE 5: When the processor is in M or S mode and menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to access mhpmevent16 through a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: When the processor is in M or S mode, any attempt to access mhpmevent16 via sireg3 or sireg6 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When the processor is in M or S mode and XLEN = 64, any attempt to access mhpmevent16 via sireg4 or sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: When the processor is in M or S mode and siselect = 0x41, any attempt to access mhpmevent16 through a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: When the processor is in M or S mode and the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), any attempt to access mhpmevent16 through a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If any extension required for the state of mhpmevent16 is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent16 through a sireg* register raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent16.OF bit is one of the mhpmevent n . OF bits that can cause the sip.LCOFIP bit to reflect a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 12: If the mhpmevent16.OF bit is set, a local-counter-overflow interrupt request occurs.
RULE 13: When a local-counter-overflow interrupt request occurs because the mhpmevent16.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit may be set to reflect that occurrence.
RULE 14: The OF field of mhpmevent16 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 15: The MINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 16: The SINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 17: The UINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in U-mode.
RULE 18: The VSINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in VS-mode.
RULE 19: The VUINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in VU-mode.
RULE 20: The two WPRI fields of mhpmevent16 are reserved.
RULE 21: Each INH bit in mhpmevent16 (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) reads as zero and is read-only when the corresponding privilege mode is not implemented.
RULE 22: When any INH bit of mhpmevent16 is set, it inhibits event counting in the corresponding privilege mode, and when all INH bits are zero, event counting is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 23: The OF bit of mhpmevent16 is set when hpmcounter16 overflows and remains set until software writes to mhpmevent16 to clear it.
RULE 24: Overflow of hpmcounter16, defined as unsigned overflow of its implemented bits, causes the OF bit of mhpmevent16 to become sticky while the counter continues to wrap around.
RULE 25: When supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent16.
RULE 26: If hpmcounter16 overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent16 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated, making the OF bit an interrupt-disable flag.
RULE 27: Writes to mhpmevent16 never cause a count overflow; count overflow occurs only from hardware increments of hpmcounter16.
RULE 28: A count-overflow interrupt request associated with the OF bit of mhpmevent16 is signaled via the LCOFIP pending bit (bit 13) in the mip and sip registers and is enabled by the LCOFIE bits in the mie and sie registers.
RULE 29: When hpmcounter16 generates a count-overflow interrupt request, it sets the OF bit of mhpmevent16, which eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, and software must clear the LCOFIP bit before servicing the interrupt; delegation of this interrupt between S-mode and M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 30: The OF bit of mhpmevent16 serves both as overflow status and overflow-interrupt enable, requiring software to clear the OF bit and reinitialize hpmcounter16 before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 31: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent16 is mirrored in scountovf bit 16.
RULE 32: Reading the overflow bit of mhpmevent16 via scountovf bit 16 is subject to the same mcounteren (and hcounteren, when applicable) CSR permissions that control access to the hpmcounter CSRs.
RULE 33: In M-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent16 is always readable.
RULE 34: In S-mode and HS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent16 is readable only when mcounteren bit 16 is set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 35: In VS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent16 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 16 and hcounteren bit 16 are set; otherwise it reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent17
NUMBER: 0x331
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf

RULE 2: mhpmevent17 is a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event which increments mhpmcounter17.
RULE 3: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event", and programming mhpmevent17 with the value 0 causes mhpmcounter17 not to increment for any event.
RULE 4: The mhpmevent17 register should be implemented in an implementation.
RULE 5: The mhpmevent17h CSR is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented; otherwise the high-half CSR for mhpmevent17 does not exist.
RULE 6: When an siselect value is associated with counter 17, the sireg or sireg2 registers can be used to access mhpmevent17.
RULE 7: When an siselect value is associated with counter 17, the sireg4 or sireg5 registers can be used to access mhpmevent17h.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent17 is accessed through a sireg* alias, bit 62 of mhpmevent17 reads as 0 and is read-only.
RULE 9: If any extension required for the state represented by mhpmevent17 is not implemented, an attempt in M or S mode to access mhpmevent17 via a sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When the processor is in M or S mode, siselect selects mhpmevent17 (value in the range 0x40-0x5F), and menvcfg.CDE is 0, any attempt to access mhpmevent17 through a sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.

RULE 12: If XLEN is 64, an attempt to access the high-half alias of mhpmevent17 (sireg5) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mhpmevent17. OF bit contributes to a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that is reflected by the sip.LCOFIP bit.
RULE 14: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent17. OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit becomes set.
RULE 15: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE bits are read-only zeros and setting the mhpmevent17. OF bit has no effect on sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 16: The OF field of mhpmevent17 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the corresponding counter overflows.
RULE 17: The MINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 18: The SINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 19: The UINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 20: The VSINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual supervisor mode.
RULE 21: The VUINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual user mode.
RULE 22: For each INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent17, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented the bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 23: When any INH bit in mhpmevent17 is set, it inhibits counting of events for its corresponding privilege mode; if all INH bits are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent17 is set when hpmcounter17 overflows and remains set until software writes a value to clear it.
RULE 25: Overflow for hpmcounter17 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, which triggers the OF bit in mhpmevent17.
RULE 26: After an overflow, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent17 remains set, preserving overflow information.
RULE 27: If hpmcounter17 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent17 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: If the OF bit in mhpmevent17 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent17 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter17.
RULE 30: Writes to mhpmevent17 cannot cause a counter overflow because overflow only results from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 31: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter17 is presented as a standard local interrupt mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 32: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow interrupt, and the LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 33: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter17 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent17.
RULE 34: When the OF bit in mhpmevent17 becomes set, it eventually causes the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers to be set, though the propagation need not be immediate.
RULE 35: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt is delegated to supervisor mode or remains handled in machine mode.
RULE 36: Reading the OF bit of mhpmevent17 via scountovf is subject to the same mcounteren (and hcounteren for VS-mode) permission checks that apply to hpmcounter17 accesses.
RULE 37: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent17 is always readable through scountovf.
RULE 38: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent17 is readable through scountovf only when mcounteren bit 17 is set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 39: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent17 is readable through scountovf only when both mcounteren bit 17 and hcounteren bit 17 are set, otherwise the read returns zero.

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent20 may cause the mip.LCOFIP bit to become set, reflecting the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 2: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit of mhpmevent20.
RULE 3: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero and setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent20 does not cause any change in mip.LCOFIP.
RULE 4: mhpmevent20 is a 64-bit WARL register.
RULE 5: mhpmevent20 controls which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter20 to increment.
RULE 6: For mhpmevent20, an event value of 0 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 7: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent20 read-only zero.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a high-half CSR named mhpmevent20h provides access to bits 63-32 of mhpmevent20.
RULE 9: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a read of mhpmevent20h returns bits 63-32 of mhpmevent20.
RULE 10: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a write to mhpmevent20h changes only bits 63-32 of mhpmevent20.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent20 accessed through a sireg* alias is read-only 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 12: When executing in M or S privilege mode and siselect = 0x41, any attempt to read or write mhpmevent20 through a sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When executing in M or S privilege mode with siselect in the range 0x40-0x5F and the bit for mhpmevent20 in mcounteren is 0, any attempt to read or write mhpmevent20 through a sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: If the menvcfg.CDE bit is 0, any access to mhpmevent20 via the delegated-counter alias registers (sireg*) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If XLEN is 64, any access to mhpmevent20 through sireg4 or sireg5 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: If mstateen0[60] = 0 or hstateen0[60] = 0, access to mhpmevent20 as a CSR is blocked.
RULE 17: If any extension on which the underlying state of mhpmevent20 depends is not implemented, any M-mode or S-mode access to mhpmevent20 through a sireg* alias raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit is a read-write field that reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent20.OF bit being set.
RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent20.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit will indicate that a local-counter-overflow interrupt request has occurred.
RULE 20: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE bits are read-only zeros regardless of the state of the mhpmevent20.OF bit.
RULE 21: The OF field in mhpmevent20 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 22: The OF bit in mhpmevent20 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 23: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 24: The MINH bit in mhpmevent20, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in machine mode.
RULE 25: The SINH bit in mhpmevent20, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 26: The UINH bit in mhpmevent20, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in user mode.
RULE 27: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent20, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 28: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent20, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in virtual-user mode.
RULE 29: If all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent20 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 30: For any INH bit in mhpmevent20 whose associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 31: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent20 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: If the OF bit of mhpmevent20 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 33: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the associated hpmcounter sets the OF bit of mhpmevent20.
RULE 34: When the OF bit of mhpmevent20 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 35: The LCOFIP bit in mip or sip and the LCOFIE bit in mie or sie serve as the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits, respectively, for the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent20.
RULE 36: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent20 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 37: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent20 is performed by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing the corresponding counter to a starting value.
RULE 38: After the counter associated with mhpmevent20 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 39: Writes to mhpmevent20 never cause a counter overflow; overflow can only occur from hardware increments of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 40: mhpmevent20 includes an overflow bit designated OF.
RULE 41: The OF bit in mhpmevent20 is shadow-copied into bit 20 of the read-only scountovf CSR.

REGISTER: mhpmevent21
NUMBER: 0x335
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent21 contains an overflow flag bit named .OF.
RULE 2: The .OF bit of mhpmevent21 is included among the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting can cause the mip.LCOFIP field to indicate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: When the .OF bit of mhpmevent21 is set, it directly contributes to the condition that causes mip.LCOFIP to indicate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 4: The mip.LCOFIP field reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the .OF bit of mhpmevent21 being set.
RULE 5: The influence of the .OF bit of mhpmevent21 on mip.LCOFIP is unchanged even if the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented.
RULE 6: mhpmevent21 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter21 to increment.
RULE 7: Event 0 encoded in mhpmevent21 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 8: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent21 read-only 0 together with its counter as an alternative to implementing the counter.
RULE 9: When a siselect value that selects counter 21 is programmed, the mhpmevent21 CSR may be accessed through the sireg or sireg2 indirect registers.
RULE 10: When the same siselect value that selects counter 21 is programmed, the high-word CSR mhpmevent21h may be accessed through the sireg4 or sireg5 indirect registers.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent21 register is accessed indirectly through a sireg* alias, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent21 must read as 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 12: If any extension required for the underlying state of mhpmevent21 is not implemented, any attempt in M or S mode to access mhpmevent21 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: While executing in M or S mode with siselect holding a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent21 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 14: While executing in M or S mode with siselect holding a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent21 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if the accessed sireg* is sireg3 or sireg6.
RULE 15: While executing in M or S mode with siselect holding a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent21 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if the accessed sireg* is sireg4 or sireg5 and XLEN = 64.
RULE 16: While executing in M or S mode with siselect holding a value in the range 0x40-0x5F, an attempt to access mhpmevent21 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if siselect = 0x41 or if the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0).
RULE 17: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent21 contributes to the condition that can cause the sip.LCOFIP interrupt-pending bit to become set.
RULE 18: The .OF bit of mhpmevent21 is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting is reflected by sip.LCOFIP as a local counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the .OF bit of mhpmevent21 has no effect because sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 20: In mhpmevent21, bit 63 named OF is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 21: In mhpmevent21, bit 62 named MINH inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode when set.
RULE 22: In mhpmevent21, bit 61 named SINH inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 23: In mhpmevent21, bit 60 named UINH inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode when set.
RULE 24: In mhpmevent21, bit 59 named VSINH inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode when set.
RULE 25: In mhpmevent21, bit 58 named VUINH inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode when set.
RULE 26: For each INH bit in mhpmevent21, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 27: When any x INH bit in mhpmevent21 is set, counting of events in privilege mode x is inhibited, and if all INH bits are zero counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 28: The OF bit in mhpmevent21 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: In mhpmevent21 overflow is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 30: After an overflow, the counter associated with mhpmevent21 wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, so no information is lost.
RULE 31: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent21 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: If the OF bit in mhpmevent21 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: The OF bit in mhpmevent21 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 34: Count overflow for mhpmevent21 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments of the counter register.
RULE 35: A count-overflow interrupt generated by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent21 is presented as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 36: The LCOFIP and LCOFIE bits in mip/sip and mie/sie, respectively, are the pending and enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent21.
RULE 37: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent21 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent21.
RULE 38: When the OF bit in mhpmevent21 is set, the LCOFIP pending bit in mip/sip will eventually be set.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent21 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 40: There are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmevent21; enabling overflow interrupt generation is done by clearing the OF bit while initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 41: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent21 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 42: scountovf bit 21 is a shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent21.
RULE 43: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent21 can always be read via scountovf bit 21.
RULE 44: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent21 can be read via scountovf bit 21 only if mcounteren bit 21 is set; otherwise scountovf bit 21 reads as zero.
RULE 45: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent21 can be read via scountovf bit 21 only if both mcounteren bit 21 and hcounteren bit 21 are set; otherwise scountovf bit 21 reads as zero.
RULE 46: Read access to scountovf bit 21 is governed by the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) CSR permissions that control access to the hpmcounter CSRs by S-mode (or VS-mode).

REGISTER: mhpmevent22
NUMBER: 0x336
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent22 is a 64-bit WARL CSR that selects the event which causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter22 to increment.
RULE 2: The architectural definition of event value 0 for mhpmevent22 is "no event".
RULE 3: A write to mhpmevent22 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent22 read-only and return zero for all reads.
RULE 5: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, then bit 62 (MINH) of the mhpmevent22 register is read-only and reads as zero when the mhpmevent22 state is accessed via the indirect sireg* CSRs.
RULE 6: The mhpmevent22. OF bit, when set, contributes to the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 7: If the mhpmevent22. OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit becomes set.
RULE 8: The OF field of mhpmevent22 indicates overflow status and acts as an interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 9: The MINH field of mhpmevent22, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 10: The SINH field of mhpmevent22, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.

RULE 12: The VSINH field of mhpmevent22, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in virtual supervisor mode.

RULE 14: If a privilege mode associated with an x INH bit in mhpmevent22 is not implemented, that x INH bit is read-only zero.

RULE 16: The OF bit in mhpmevent22 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes the bit.
RULE 17: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, after which the counter wraps and continues counting while the sticky OF bit stays set.
RULE 18: When supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit from mhpmevent22.
RULE 19: If the OF bit in mhpmevent22 is zero when its associated hpmcounter overflows, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If the OF bit in mhpmevent22 is one when its associated hpmcounter overflows, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent22 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 22: Writing to mhpmevent22 does not cause a count overflow because overflow can only result from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 23: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal generated by an hpmcounter is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 24: The mip and sip registers contain an LCOFIP bit that indicates the pending state of the count-overflow interrupt, while the mie and sie registers contain an LCOFIE bit that enables the interrupt.
RULE 25: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by an hpmcounter sets the OF bit in mhpmevent22.
RULE 26: When the OF bit in mhpmevent22 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 27: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent22 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 28: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent22 is accomplished by clearing its OF bit while initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 29: After mhpmevent22 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 30: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent22 (accessed via scountovf bit 22) is always readable.
RULE 31: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent22 (accessed via scountovf bit 22) is readable only when mcounteren bit 22 is set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 32: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent22 (accessed via scountovf bit 22) is readable only when both mcounteren bit 22 and hcounteren bit 22 are set, otherwise it reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent23

MODE: M-mode

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent23 register includes an .OF bit that functions as an overflow flag.
RULE 2: Setting the mhpmevent23 .OF bit contributes to the condition that may cause a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.

RULE 4: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the setting of the mhpmevent23 .OF bit cannot result in any local-counter-overflow interrupt request being signaled.
RULE 5: The state of the mie.LCOFIE interrupt-enable bit does not affect the setting of the mhpmevent23 .OF bit.
RULE 6: mhpmevent23 is a 64-bit WARL CSR that selects the event for counter mhpmcounter23.
RULE 7: In mhpmevent23, an event value of 0 denotes "no event".
RULE 8: Any CSR write to mhpmevent23 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 9: When the siselect register holds the value associated with counter 23, the sireg2 register can be used to access mhpmevent23.
RULE 10: An implementation may raise an illegal-instruction exception when siselect holds a non-implemented value and an access to a sireg* register for mhpmevent23 is attempted.

RULE 12: When mcounteren[23] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1, the state of mhpmevent23 may be read or written via sireg* while siselect holds the value 0x57.

RULE 18: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, then sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero and setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent23 cannot cause sip.LCOFIP to become 1.
RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, then sie.LCOFIE is a read-only zero and setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent23 cannot enable a local counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 20: The OF field of mhpmevent23 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 21: When the MINH bit of mhpmevent23 is set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 22: When the SINH bit of mhpmevent23 is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.

RULE 34: No count-overflow interrupt request is generated when the OF bit of mhpmevent23 is one at the time of overflow.
RULE 35: The OF bit of mhpmevent23 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for its associated hpmcounter.
RULE 36: Count overflow for the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent23 occurs only from hardware increments, never from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers.

RULE 38: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip and the LCOFIE bit in mie/sie serve as the pending and enable bits, respectively, for the count-overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent23.
RULE 39: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent23, the OF bit of mhpmevent23 is set.
RULE 40: Setting the OF bit of mhpmevent23 eventually causes the LCOFIP bit in mip/sip to be set, though not necessarily immediately.

REGISTER: mhpmevent24

RULE 6: Event code 0 in mhpmevent24 denotes "no event", meaning the associated counter will not be incremented for any event.
RULE 7: A legal implementation may implement mhpmevent24 as a read-only register that always returns 0.

RULE 14: If any extension required for the underlying state of mhpmevent24 (such as Sscofpmf for the MINH bit) is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent24 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: When the hypervisor (H) extension is implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent24 via vsireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the OF bit in mhpmevent24 may cause sip.LCOFIP to become 1, indicating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
