RULE 19: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the OF bit in mhpmevent24 does not affect sip.LCOFIP, which remains a read-only zero.
RULE 20: Because sip.LCOFIP is writable when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, software can clear a pending interrupt generated by the mhpmevent24.OF bit by writing 0 to sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent24 is one of the mhpmevent<n>.OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 22: The OF bit (bit 63) of mhpmevent24 indicates overflow status and disables the interrupt when set, and it is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 23: The MINH bit (bit 62) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode when set.
RULE 24: The SINH bit (bit 61) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 25: The UINH bit (bit 60) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode when set.
RULE 26: The VSINH bit (bit 59) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode when set.
RULE 27: The VUINH bit (bit 58) of mhpmevent24 inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode when set.
RULE 28: Bits 57-56 of mhpmevent24 are reserved (WPRI).
RULE 29: For each INH bit in mhpmevent24, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 30: When any INH bit in mhpmevent24 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 31: If all INH bits in mhpmevent24 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 32: The OF bit of mhpmevent24 remains set until written by software.
RULE 33: Overflow of the counter paired with mhpmevent24 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 34: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 35: If the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 36: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the counter paired with mhpmevent24 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent24.
RULE 37: When the OF bit of mhpmevent24 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 38: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent24 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 39: Writing mhpmevent24 does not cause a counter overflow; count overflow only results from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 40: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmevent24; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing the counter.
RULE 41: Once the counter paired with mhpmevent24 has overflowed, it and the OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 42: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is mirrored in scountovf bit 24.
RULE 43: In M-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is always readable via scountovf bit 24.
RULE 44: In S-mode or HS-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is readable via scountovf bit 24 only when the corresponding mcounteren bit 24 is set; otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 45: In VS-mode, the overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent24 is readable via scountovf bit 24 only when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 24 and hcounteren bit 24 are set; otherwise it reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent25
NUMBER: 0x339
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The privilege of mhpmevent25 is MRW, meaning it is a machine-mode CSR that can be read and written by privileged software.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mhpmevent25 register contains an .OF bit that serves as the overflow flag for that event.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent25 .OF bit is set, the mip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request caused by that set .OF bit.
RULE 4: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mie.LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit corresponding to the mip.LCOFIP bit.
RULE 6: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit (and all other mhpmevent n .OF bits) do not affect any architectural state.
RULE 7: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit does not affect any architectural state, and the mip.LCOFIP bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 8: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mhpmevent25 .OF bit does not affect any architectural state, and the mie.LCOFIE bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 9: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent25 selects the "no event" condition for mhpmcounter25.
RULE 10: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent25 read-only with the fixed value 0.
RULE 11: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent25 is accessed through the delegated alias registers (sireg*), event selector bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent25 is read-only 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 12: If any extension on which the underlying state of mhpmevent25 depends is not implemented, any access to mhpmevent25 via sireg* from M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: The mhpmevent25 register contains an OF bit that, when set, indicates that a local-counter-overflow interrupt request has occurred.
RULE 14: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent25.OF bit may cause the sip.LCOFIP bit to become 1, reflecting the local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 15: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit is hard-wired to zero, and setting the mhpmevent25.OF bit does not affect sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 16: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH) is not implemented, the respective INH bit in mhpmevent25 is read-only zero.
RULE 17: When any of the INH bits MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, or VUINH in mhpmevent25 is set, event counting is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if all these INH bits are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent25 is set when its associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes to clear it.
RULE 19: Overflow for the OF bit in mhpmevent25 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented bits of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 20: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent25 overflows while the mhpmevent25 OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent25 overflows while the mhpmevent25 OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 22: Overflow of the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent25 never occurs as a result of writes to mhpmcounter25 or mhpmevent25 registers, and can only result from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 23: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by an overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent25 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 24: For the overflow interrupt of mhpmevent25, the LCOFIP bit in mip or sip is the interrupt-pending bit and the LCOFIE bit in mie or sie is the interrupt-enable bit.
RULE 25: When a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent25, the mhpmevent25 OF bit is set.
RULE 26: When the OF bit in mhpmevent25 becomes set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 27: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent25 to supervisor mode or machine mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 28: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent25 is achieved by clearing its OF bit while initializing the associated counter to a starting value.
RULE 29: After the counter associated with mhpmevent25 has overflowed, both the counter and the mhpmevent25 OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 30: The overflow (OF) bit in mhpmevent25 is duplicated in scountovf bit 25.
RULE 31: In M-mode, a read of scountovf bit 25 (which duplicates the OF bit of mhpmevent25) always returns the current value of that OF bit.
RULE 32: In S-mode or HS-mode, a read of scountovf bit 25 returns the current OF bit value of mhpmevent25 only when mcounteren bit 25 is set; otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 33: In VS-mode, a read of scountovf bit 25 returns the current OF bit value of mhpmevent25 only when both mcounteren bit 25 and hcounteren bit 25 are set; otherwise the read returns zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent26
NUMBER: 0x33a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The privilege level for mhpmevent26 is machine-read/write (MRW).
RULE 2: The privilege level for mhpmevent26h is machine-read/write (MRW).
RULE 3: mhpmevent26 is a 64-bit WARL register that belongs to the set of event selector CSRs mhpmevent3-mhpmevent31.
RULE 4: Event 0 in mhpmevent26 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 5: The value written to mhpmevent26 selects the hardware event that causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter26 to increment.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may implement mhpmevent26 as a read-only register that always returns 0.
RULE 7: Any write to mhpmevent26 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: If any extension required by the state accessed through mhpmevent26 is not implemented, then an access to that state via a system register (sireg) from M mode or S mode MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: The mhpmevent26 register contains an OF bit that, when set, contributes to generating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 10: When the mhpmevent26.OF bit is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit will indicate the resulting overflow interrupt request.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent26 register bits 63–56 are defined as OF, MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH, and two reserved WPRI bits.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 13: The MINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 14: The SINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 15: The UINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 16: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 17: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent26, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 18: The two WPRI bits in mhpmevent26 are reserved.
RULE 19: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent26 is not implemented, that INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 20: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent26 are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes; when any INH bit is set, counting is inhibited for its corresponding mode.
RULE 21: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 is set by hardware on unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, remains set until written by software, and indicates that the counter has wrapped around without loss of information.
RULE 22: The OF bit in mhpmevent26 disables generation of a count-overflow interrupt request when it is set; if it is clear at the time of overflow, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: Writes to mhpmevent26 never cause a count overflow; count overflow can occur only from hardware increments of the associated counter.
RULE 24: A count-overflow interrupt generated due to overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent26 is signaled via local interrupt bit 13 (LCOFIP/LCOFIE) in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 25: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by the counter associated with mhpmevent26, hardware sets the OF bit in mhpmevent26, which eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, and software must clear the LCOFIP bit before servicing the interrupt; delegation of this interrupt is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 26: After the counter associated with mhpmevent26 has overflowed, software must reinitialize both the counter and the OF bit before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 27: The scountovf CSR bit 26 is a shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent26.
RULE 28: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is always readable via the scountovf CSR.
RULE 29: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is readable via the scountovf CSR when the corresponding mcounteren bit 26 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 30: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent26 is readable via the scountovf CSR when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 26 and hcounteren bit 26 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.

RULE 7: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event", therefore programming mhpmevent27 with the value 0 causes mhpmcounter27 to never increment for any event.

RULE 18: The implementation of the H extension prevents VS-mode from using the indirect mapping (siselect = 0x5B) to access mhpmevent27 via vsireg.
RULE 19: The OF field of mhpmevent27 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.

RULE 21: If the SINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.

RULE 23: If the VSINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in VS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 24: If the VUINH bit of mhpmevent27 is set, counting of events in VU-mode is inhibited.

RULE 30: When the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is set, the counter continues to wrap around and count while the sticky OF bit remains set, so overflow does not lose information.

RULE 32: If the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.

RULE 37: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent27 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent27.
RULE 38: When the OF bit of mhpmevent27 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent27 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 40: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent27 has overflowed, it and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 41: In M-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are always permitted.
RULE 42: In S-mode or HS-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are permitted only when mcounteren bit 27 is set, and otherwise return zero.
RULE 43: In VS-mode, reads of the scountovf shadow of mhpmevent27's OF bit (bit 27) are permitted only when both mcounteren bit 27 and hcounteren bit 27 are set, and otherwise return zero.

RULE 16: If the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated for an overflow of hpmcounter29.
RULE 17: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated for hpmcounter29, the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is set.
RULE 18: After the OF bit in mhpmevent29 is set by a count-overflow interrupt request, the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers is eventually set but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 19: The mideleg register controls delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter29, which is the interrupt associated with the OF bit in mhpmevent29.
RULE 20: Writes to mhpmevent29 do not cause a count overflow; count overflow only results from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 21: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter29 is performed by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent29 in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 22: After hpmcounter29 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent29 MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 23: The MINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in machine mode.
RULE 24: The SINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in supervisor/hypervisor mode.
RULE 25: The UINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in user mode.
RULE 26: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in virtual-supervisor mode.
RULE 27: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent29, when set, inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter29 in virtual-user mode.
RULE 28: If all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent29 are zero, counting of events for hpmcounter29 occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: For each INH bit in mhpmevent29, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.
RULE 30: The scountovf CSR bit 29 holds a shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent29.
RULE 31: In M-mode, the shadow copy of mhpmevent29's OF bit stored in scountovf bit 29 is always readable.
RULE 32: In S-mode or HS-mode, the shadow copy of mhpmevent29's OF bit stored in scountovf bit 29 is readable only when the corresponding mcounteren bit 29 is set, otherwise a read of that bit returns zero.
RULE 33: In VS-mode, the shadow copy of mhpmevent29's OF bit stored in scountovf bit 29 is readable only when both the corresponding mcounteren bit 29 and hcounteren bit 29 are set, otherwise a read of that bit returns zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent3
NUMBER: 0x323
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent3 register is accessible with machine read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The LCOFIP bit in the mip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the OF bit of mhpmevent3 being set.
RULE 3: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set to indicate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 4: The LCOFIE bit in the mie register controls whether an interrupt request indicated by the LCOFIP bit, which may be caused by the OF bit of mhpmevent3, can trap.
RULE 5: mhpmevent3 is a 64-bit WARL register that selects the event that causes its corresponding performance counter to increment.
RULE 6: Setting mhpmevent3 to the value 0 selects the defined "no event".
RULE 7: A legal implementation is permitted to make mhpmevent3 a read-only register that always returns zero.
RULE 8: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent3 register is accessed through the sireg* CSRs (siselect = 0x43, sireg2), event selector bit 62 (MINH) reads as 0 and cannot be written.
RULE 9: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent3 may cause the sip.LCOFIP bit to become set, reflecting a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 10: The .OF bit of mhpmevent3 reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request when it is set.
RULE 11: The OF bit in mhpmevent3 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 12: The MINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 13: The SINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 14: The UINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 15: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 16: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 17: The two WPRI bits in mhpmevent3 are reserved.
RULE 18: For each INH bit in mhpmevent3, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 19: If all INH bits in mhpmevent3 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 20: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 21: After overflow, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the OF bit in mhpmevent3 remains set.
RULE 22: If supervisor mode is implemented, the scountovf register contains a read-only shadow copy of the OF bit of mhpmevent3.
RULE 23: If the associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: The OF bit of mhpmevent3 functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 26: Writes to mhpmevent3 never cause a count overflow; count overflow can only result from hardware increments of the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 27: The count overflow interrupt request generated by the associated hpmcounter is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 28: The LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register is the interrupt-pending bit for the count overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent3.
RULE 29: The LCOFIE bit in the mie or sie register is the interrupt-enable bit for the count overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent3.
RULE 30: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by the associated hpmcounter sets the OF bit in mhpmevent3.
RULE 31: When the OF bit in mhpmevent3 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 32: The mideleg register controls whether the count overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent3 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 33: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent3 is done by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent3 in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 34: After the counter associated with mhpmevent3 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent3 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 35: For mhpmevent3, scountovf bit 3 is the shadow copy of the OF bit in mhpmevent3.
RULE 36: In M-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent3 as reflected in scountovf bit 3 is always readable.
RULE 37: In S-mode and HS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent3 as reflected in scountovf bit 3 is readable only when mcounteren bit 3 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 38: In VS-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent3 as reflected in scountovf bit 3 is readable only when both mcounteren bit 3 and hcounteren bit 3 are set, and otherwise reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent30

RULE 2: The LCOFIP bit in the mip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit of mhpmevent30.
RULE 3: When mhpmevent30 is programmed with the value 0, it selects no event.
RULE 4: A legal implementation may make mhpmevent30 read-only 0.
RULE 5: Any write to the mhpmevent30 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: An illegal-instruction exception may be raised when an indirect access to mhpmevent30 is attempted via mireg* while miselect holds a non-implemented value.
RULE 7: An indirect access to mhpmevent30 via a mireg i may result in accessing the register state, accessing a read-only zero state, or raising an illegal-instruction exception, depending on the defining extension.
RULE 8: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent30 is accessed through a sireg* CSR, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent30 reads as 0 and is read-only.

RULE 11: If the privilege mode is M or S and siselect = 0x41, then an attempt to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: If the privilege mode is M or S, siselect is in the range 0x40-0x5F, and the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), then an attempt to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If any extension required for the state accessed by mhpmevent30 is not implemented, then an attempt in M or S mode to access mhpmevent30 via a sireg* CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 indicates overflow status and disables the overflow interrupt when set.
RULE 15: The MINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 16: The SINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 17: The UINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 18: The VSINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VS-mode.
RULE 19: The VUINH bit in mhpmevent30, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in VU-mode.
RULE 20: The WPRI bits in mhpmevent30 are reserved.
RULE 21: If a privilege mode associated with an INH bit in mhpmevent30 is not implemented, that INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 22: When any INH bit in mhpmevent30 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if all INH bits are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 23: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 24: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent30 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: If the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: The OF bit in mhpmevent30 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 27: Count overflow for the counter linked to mhpmevent30 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter or mhpmevent registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 28: The count overflow interrupt request generated by the OF bit of mhpmevent30 is treated as a standard local interrupt mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 29: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits, and the LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt associated with mhpmevent30.
RULE 30: Generation of a count overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent30 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent30.
RULE 31: When the OF bit in mhpmevent30 is set, the LCOFIP bit in mip and sip is eventually set, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 32: The delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent30 to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 33: After the counter linked to mhpmevent30 overflows, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent30 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 34: The overflow (OF) bit of mhpmevent30 is mirrored in scountovf bit 30.
RULE 35: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is always readable.
RULE 36: In S-mode and HS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is readable only when mcounteren bit 30 is set, otherwise it reads as zero.
RULE 37: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent30 (accessed via scountovf bit 30) is readable only when both mcounteren bit 30 and hcounteren bit 30 are set, otherwise it reads as zero.

REGISTER: mhpmevent31

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent31 CSR is accessible with machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the mhpmevent31.OF bit is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIE bit in the mie register is the interrupt-enable for the local-counter-overflow interrupt that can be generated by setting mhpmevent31.OF.
RULE 4: The local-counter-overflow interrupt is pending only if the LCOFIP bit in mip reflects the occurrence of setting mhpmevent31.OF and the LCOFIE bit in mie is set.
RULE 5: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mip.LCOFIP and mie.LCOFIE bits are read-only zeros, so they never reflect a change caused by mhpmevent31.OF.
RULE 6: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, setting the mhpmevent31.OF bit does not cause any architectural effect and no local-counter-overflow interrupt is generated.
RULE 7: mhpmevent31 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes the corresponding counter to increment.
RULE 8: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event" for mhpmevent31.

RULE 10: The mhpmevent31 register can be accessed indirectly via the sireg2 CSR when the siselect field is set to 0x5F.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent31 is read-only and reads as 0 when the register is accessed through any sireg*.

RULE 15: If any architectural extension required for the state of mhpmevent31 is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access mhpmevent31 via sireg2 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: The .OF bit of mhpmevent31 is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 17: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 contributes to the condition that any mhpmevent n .OF bit is set, thereby generating a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 18: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 causes the sip.LCOFIP bit to be set, and sip.LCOFIP is a read-write bit.
RULE 19: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero, so setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent31 does not affect sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 20: The sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that results from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit of mhpmevent31.
RULE 21: If a privilege mode corresponding to an x INH bit in mhpmevent31 is not implemented, that x INH bit is read-only zero.
RULE 22: When set, each of the five x INH bits in mhpmevent31 inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in the corresponding privilege mode x.
RULE 23: When all five x INH bits in mhpmevent31 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent31 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 25: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 26: If the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 27: The OF bit in mhpmevent31 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 28: Count overflow for the counter linked to mhpmevent31 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, only from hardware increments of the counter registers.
RULE 29: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter sets the OF bit in mhpmevent31.
RULE 30: When the OF bit in mhpmevent31 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 31: Enabling overflow interrupt generation is accomplished by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent31 together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 32: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent31 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent31 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: The scountovf CSR contains a shadow copy of the OF (overflow) bit of mhpmevent31.
RULE 34: Bit 31 of the scountovf CSR corresponds to the OF bit of mhpmevent31.

RULE 43: The OF bit of mhpmevent5 is mirrored as bit 5 of the read-only scountovf CSR.
RULE 44: In M-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is always readable.
RULE 45: In S-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is readable only if mcounteren bit 5 is set, otherwise a read returns zero.
RULE 46: In VS-mode, the OF bit of mhpmevent5 (accessed via its scountovf shadow) is readable only if both mcounteren bit 5 and hcounteren bit 5 are set, otherwise a read returns zero.

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: When mhpmevent6 is programmed with the value 0, no event will cause mhpmcounter6 to increment because event 0 is defined as "no event".

RULE 6: When executing in M or S mode with siselect = 0x46, an attempt to read or write mhpmevent6 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0.
RULE 7: When executing in M or S mode with siselect = 0x46, an attempt to read or write mhpmevent6 via sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception if mcounteren[6] = 0.

RULE 10: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and mhpmevent6.OF is set, the sip.LCOFIP bit becomes set.
RULE 11: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the sie.LCOFIE bit is defined and enables the local-counter-overflow interrupt that can be triggered by mhpmevent6.OF.
RULE 12: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero and setting mhpmevent6.OF does not cause any change to sip.LCOFIP.
RULE 13: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sie.LCOFIE is a read-only zero and setting mhpmevent6.OF does not cause any change to sie.LCOFIE.

RULE 15: Bit 62 (MINH) of mhpmevent6, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 16: Bit 61 (SINH) of mhpmevent6, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in S/HS-mode.
RULE 17: Bit 60 (UINH) of mhpmevent6, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 18: Bit 59 (VSINH) of mhpmevent6, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VS-mode.
RULE 19: Bit 58 (VUINH) of mhpmevent6, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in VU-mode.
RULE 20: Bits 57-56 of mhpmevent6 are reserved (WPRI).
RULE 21: For each x INH bit in mhpmevent6, if the associated privilege mode x is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.

RULE 23: All zero values for the x INH bits in mhpmevent6 result in counting of events in all modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 25: Overflow of the corresponding hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent6 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 26: There is no loss of information after an overflow because the counter wraps around and the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent6 remains set.
RULE 27: If an hpmcounter overflows while the associated OF bit in mhpmevent6 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: If the OF bit in mhpmevent6 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 29: The OF bit in mhpmevent6 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 30: Writes to mhpmevent6 do not cause overflow because count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 31: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent6 is done by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 32: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent6 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: The mhpmevent6 CSR contains an overflow (OF) bit that may be shadowed by the scountovf CSR.

REGISTER: mideleg
NUMBER: 0x303
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSI, 2..2=VSSI, 3..3=MSI, 5..5=STI, 6..6=VSTI, 7..7=MTI, 9..9=SEI, 10..10=VSEI, 11..11=MEI, 12..12=SGEI, 13..13=LCOFI
EXTENSIONS: H, S, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mideleg register is accessible in machine privilege mode for both read and write operations (MRW).
RULE 2: The mideleg register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: In harts that implement S-mode, the mideleg register must exist.
RULE 4: In harts that implement S-mode, setting a bit in mideleg delegates the corresponding trap that occurs in S-mode or U-mode to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 5: In harts that do not implement S-mode, the mideleg register should not exist.
RULE 6: An implementation may support only a subset of delegatable traps, and the supported delegatable bits in mideleg can be discovered by writing one to every bit position of mideleg and then reading back the value to see which bit positions retain a one.
RULE 7: If the supervisor timer interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting mideleg[5], the supervisor timer interrupt will not be taken while executing in M-mode.
RULE 8: If mideleg[5] is clear, the supervisor timer interrupt can be taken in any mode and will always transfer control to M-mode regardless of the current mode.
RULE 9: The delegation control for the supervisor timer interrupt is located in bit 5 of mideleg.
RULE 10: An interrupt i traps to M-mode only if, when the mideleg register exists, bit i in mideleg is clear.
RULE 11: Setting a bit in the mideleg register delegates the corresponding interrupt to S-mode, making the interrupt visible in the sip register.
RULE 12: Setting a bit in the mideleg register makes the corresponding interrupt maskable via the sie register.
RULE 13: If a bit in the mideleg register is not set, the corresponding bits in sip and sie are read-only zero.
RULE 14: The LCOFI bit (bit 13) in the mideleg CSR, when set, delegates all LCOFIs to S-mode.
RULE 15: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt is delegated to S-mode or remains handled in M-mode.
RULE 16: The count-overflow interrupt that mideleg delegates is the local count overflow interrupt represented by bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 17: An interrupt that has been delegated to HS-mode using mideleg is further delegated to VS-mode if the corresponding hideleg bit is set.
RULE 18: When a virtual supervisor external interrupt (code 10) is delegated to HS-mode using mideleg and then delegated to VS-mode, the machine automatically translates it into a supervisor external interrupt (code 9) for VS-mode and includes the value written to vscause on the interrupt trap.
RULE 19: When a virtual supervisor timer interrupt (code 6) is delegated to HS-mode using mideleg and then delegated to VS-mode, the machine translates it into a supervisor timer interrupt (code 5) for VS-mode.
RULE 20: When a virtual supervisor software interrupt (code 2) is delegated to HS-mode using mideleg and then delegated to VS-mode, the machine translates it into a supervisor software interrupt (code 1) for VS-mode.
RULE 21: When the hypervisor extension is implemented, bits 10, 6, and 2 of mideleg are each read-only one.
RULE 22: For any bit of mideleg that is zero, the corresponding bits in hideleg, hip, and hie are read-only zeros.
RULE 23: If a trap occurring in HS-mode or U-mode is delegated by mideleg, the trap is taken to HS-mode instead of M-mode.
RULE 24: If a trap occurring in HS-mode or U-mode is not delegated by mideleg (and not delegated by medeleg), the trap is taken to M-mode.
RULE 25: If a trap occurring in VS-mode or VU-mode is not delegated by mideleg (and not delegated by medeleg), the trap is taken to M-mode.
RULE 26: If a trap occurring in VS-mode or VU-mode is delegated by mideleg (or by medeleg) and hideleg does not further delegate it, the trap is taken to HS-mode.
RULE 27: If a trap occurring in VS-mode or VU-mode is delegated by mideleg (or by medeleg) and hideleg further delegates it, the trap is taken to VS-mode.

REGISTER: mie
NUMBER: 0x304
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIE, 2..2=VSSIE, 3..3=MSIE, 5..5=STIE, 6..6=VSTIE, 7..7=MTIE, 9..9=SEIE, 10..10=VSEIE, 11..11=MEIE, 12..12=SGEIE, 13..13=LCOFIE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mie CSR is a machine-read/write (MRW) register, meaning it can be read and written when the processor is in machine privilege mode.
RULE 2: mie is an MXLEN-bit read/write register that holds interrupt enable bits.
RULE 3: For each interrupt cause number i, bit i in mie corresponds to that cause.
RULE 4: An interrupt i can trap to M-mode only if its corresponding bit i in mie is set.
RULE 5: An explicit write to mie must cause immediate evaluation of interrupt-trap conditions.
RULE 6: Any bit in mie that is not writable must read as zero.
RULE 7: In a system with only one hart, the mie.MSIE bit may be read-only zero.
RULE 8: When supervisor mode is not implemented, the mie bits SEIE, STIE, and SSIE must be read-only zero.
RULE 9: When the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, the mie.LCOFIE bit must be read-only zero.
RULE 10: For any interrupt that is not delegated to S-mode via mideleg, the corresponding bit in the supervisor-level view of mie (the sie register) is read-only zero.
RULE 11: The sip and sie registers are subsets of the mip and mie registers.
RULE 12: Reading any implemented field of sie, or writing any writable field of sie, causes a read or write of the corresponding homonymous field of mie.
RULE 13: The count overflow interrupt is treated as a standard local interrupt and is assigned to bit 13 in the mie register.
RULE 14: Bit 13 of the mie register corresponds to the count overflow interrupt, which is also mapped to the same bit position in the mip, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 15: Bit 13 in the mie register corresponds to the count-overflow-interrupt-request signal, which is treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 16: The LCOFIE bit (bit 13) in the mie register is the interrupt-enable bit for the local count overflow interrupt.
RULE 17: The delegation of the local count overflow interrupt between S-mode and M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register, which determines whether the interrupt enabled by the mie register's LCOFIE bit is taken in M-mode or delegated to S-mode.
RULE 18: Bit 15 of mie is reserved/unused and is not implemented.
RULE 19: Bit 9 of mie is reserved/unused and is implemented.
RULE 20: Bit 5 of mie is reserved/unused and is implemented.
RULE 21: Bit 1 of mie is reserved/unused and is implemented.
RULE 22: The SGEIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.
RULE 23: The VSEIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.
RULE 24: The VSTIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.
RULE 25: The VSSIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.

REGISTER: mimpid
NUMBER: 0xf13
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=Implementation
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mimpid register is a Machine-mode Read-Only (MRO) register.
RULE 2: The mimpid register must be readable in any implementation.
RULE 3: The mimpid register can return a value of 0 to indicate that the field is not implemented.

REGISTER: minstret
NUMBER: 0xb02
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscsrind
RULE 1: The minstret CSR resides at address 0xB02 and counts the number of instructions retired in machine mode.
RULE 2: The minstret CSR holds the lower 32 bits of the machine instruction-retired counter.
RULE 3: minstret CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired.
RULE 4: After a hart reset, the value of minstret is arbitrary.
RULE 5: minstret can be written with a given value.
RULE 6: A write to the minstret CSR takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: The instret CSR is a read-only shadow of the minstret register.
RULE 8: If the IR bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the instret CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception, preventing access to the minstret register.
RULE 9: If the IR bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the instret CSR are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode), allowing access to the minstret register.
RULE 10: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counters, and the minstret register continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 11: When the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 12: When the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 13: ECALL and EBREAK should not increment the minstret CSR.
RULE 14: If the MINH bit (bit 62) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in M-mode.
RULE 15: If the SINH bit (bit 61) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 16: If the UINH bit (bit 60) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in U-mode.
RULE 17: If the VSINH bit (bit 59) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in VS-mode.
RULE 18: If the VUINH bit (bit 58) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in VU-mode.
RULE 19: When all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in the minstretcfg CSR are zero, the minstret counter increments for instructions executed in any implemented privilege mode.
RULE 20: For each INH bit in positions 61 down to 58 of the minstretcfg CSR, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit reads as 0 and is read-only.
RULE 21: If the Smcdeleg and/or Ssccfg extensions are implemented, supervisor-mode code may read and write the minstretcfg CSR, subject to the INH-bit behavior.
RULE 22: The overflow (OF) bit at position 63 of the minstretcfg CSR is read-only zero, and no local-counter-overflow interrupt is generated for the minstret counter.
RULE 23: If minstretcfg is configured to inhibit a privilege mode, any instruction that retires while the CPU is executing in that inhibited mode must not increment minstret.
RULE 24: Instructions that cause a synchronous exception to a more-privileged mode are not considered to retire and must not increment minstret.
RULE 25: xRET instructions retire and should increment minstret only when the originating privilege mode is not inhibited by minstretcfg.
RULE 26: A load instruction that faults and therefore does not retire must not increment minstret.
RULE 27: Instructions executed in a privilege mode that is inhibited by minstretcfg must not increment minstret.
RULE 28: An xRET instruction that originates in a privilege mode inhibited by minstretcfg must not increment minstret even if it retires in a non-inhibited mode.
RULE 29: When a previously faulted load is re-executed and successfully retires, it must increment minstret.
RULE 30: If an instruction is emulated by software running in a privilege mode inhibited by minstretcfg, the emulation routine must increment minstret.

REGISTER: mip
NUMBER: 0x344
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIP, 2..2=VSSIP, 3..3=MSIP, 5..5=STIP, 6..6=VSTIP, 7..7=MTIP, 9..9=SEIP, 10..10=VSEIP, 11..11=MEIP, 12..12=SGEIP, 13..13=LCOFIP
EXTENSIONS: H, Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: Implicit reads of mip, such as taking an interrupt because of a change in mip, are ordered as device input.
RULE 2: mip resides in the Machine privilege level.
RULE 3: mip has access type MRW, meaning it is readable and writable in Machine mode.
RULE 4: The bit positions in the mip register have the same layout as the corresponding bit positions in the mideleg register.
RULE 5: The supervisor-timer-interrupt-pending (STIP) field is located at bit 5 of the mip register.
RULE 6: An interrupt i traps to M-mode if bit i is set in both mip and mie (together with the other conditions on mstatus and mideleg).
RULE 7: Each individual bit in mip may be either writable or read-only.
RULE 8: When a bit i in mip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to that bit.
RULE 9: mip.MEIP is read-only and is set and cleared by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 10: mip.MTIP is read-only and is cleared by writing to the memory-mapped machine-mode timer compare register.
RULE 11: mip.MSIP is read-only.
RULE 12: If supervisor mode is not implemented, the SEIP, STIP, and SSIP bits of mip are read-only zeros.
RULE 13: mip.SEIP is writable and may be written by M-mode software to indicate to S-mode that an external interrupt is pending.
RULE 14: When mip is read with a CSR instruction, the SEIP bit returned equals the logical-OR of the software bit and the external signal, and the external signal is not used to calculate the value written to SEIP.
RULE 15: Only the software-writable SEIP bit participates in the read-modify-write sequence of a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction on mip.
RULE 16: For a csrrs instruction to mip, the SEIP bit is first written with the logical-OR of the software bit and the external signal, then the software bit is updated with the logical-OR of its prior value and the source register bit.
RULE 17: For a csrrw instruction to mip, the SEIP bit is first written with the logical-OR of the software bit and the external signal, then the software bit is simply overwritten with the source register bit, and in neither case does the software bit depend on the external signal.
RULE 18: If the stimecmp register is implemented, mip.STIP is read-only and reflects the supervisor-level timer interrupt signal resulting from stimecmp, and this timer interrupt signal is cleared by writing stimecmp with a value greater than the current time value.
RULE 19: mip.SSIP is writable and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 20: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n.OF bits being set.
RULE 21: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, mip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 22: Software-interrupt pending bits are located in the lowest four bits of mip, allowing the use of a single CSR instruction with a five-bit immediate because these bits are often written by software.
RULE 23: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in mideleg, the corresponding mip bit becomes visible in the sip register and is maskable using the sie register; otherwise the corresponding bits in sip and sie are read-only zero.
RULE 24: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the STCE field in menvcfg is zero, the STIP bit in mip must behave as defined for a system in which the Sstc extension is not implemented.
RULE 25: The mip register can be interrogated to determine the presence of any interrupt in machine mode.
RULE 26: Reading any implemented field of sip causes a read of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 27: Writing any writable field of sip causes a write of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 28: The STIP bit in the mip register becomes pending whenever the unsigned integer value of time is greater than or equal to the unsigned integer value of stimecmp.
RULE 29: If the result of the unsigned comparison between time and stimecmp changes, the mip register's STIP bit is guaranteed to eventually reflect the new result, though the reflection may not be immediate.
RULE 30: The mip register's STIP bit remains set until the unsigned integer value of stimecmp becomes greater than the unsigned integer value of time, typically as a result of writing stimecmp.
RULE 31: Bit 13 of the mip register is assigned to the new count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 32: The count-overflow interrupt represented by bit 13 in the mip register is treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 33: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal is mapped to bit 13 of the mip register, where that bit represents the pending status of the Local Count Overflow Interrupt.
RULE 34: The LCOFIP field in the mip register is the interrupt-pending bit for the Local Count Overflow Interrupt.
RULE 35: When the associated OF bit becomes set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register is eventually set, though the update need not occur immediately.
RULE 36: In implementations that include the hypervisor extension, the standard portion of mip occupies bits 15 down to 0.
RULE 37: The mip bits SGEIP, VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP are aliases of the corresponding bits in the hypervisor CSR hip.
RULE 38: The alias relationship in the hypervisor CSR hip directly determines the values of the mip bits SGEIP, VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP.

REGISTER: misa
NUMBER: 0x301
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..62=MXL, 0..0=A, 1..1=B, 2..2=C, 3..3=D, 5..5=F, 6..6=G, 7..7=H, 8..8=I, 12..12=M, 16..16=Q, 18..18=S, 20..20=U, 21..21=V
EXTENSIONS: A, C, D, F, H, M, V
RULE 1: When the Zfinx extension is implemented, the misa bits F, D, and Q are hardwired to 0.
RULE 2: When mstatus.VS exists while misa.V is clear, vector emulation is enabled.
RULE 3: Implementations providing the misa register and supporting the V extension have the misa.v bit set.
RULE 4: The misa register has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege level.
RULE 5: The misa CSR is a WARL read-write register that reports the ISA supported by the hart.
RULE 6: The misa register must be readable in any implementation.
RULE 7: A value of zero may be returned from a read of misa to indicate that the misa register has not been implemented, requiring that CPU capabilities be determined through a separate non-standard mechanism.
RULE 8: The MXL field of misa is read-only.
RULE 9: The I bit in the misa Extensions field will be set for the RV32I and RV64I base ISAs.
RULE 10: The E bit in the misa Extensions field will be set for the RV32E and RV64E base ISAs.
RULE 11: The Extensions field of misa is a WARL field that can contain writable bits where the implementation allows the supported ISA to be modified.
RULE 12: At reset, the Extensions field of misa shall contain the maximal set of supported extensions, and the I bit shall be selected over the E bit if both are available.
RULE 13: When a standard extension is disabled by clearing its bit in misa, the instructions and CSRs defined or modified by that extension revert to their defined or reserved behaviors as if the extension is not implemented.
RULE 14: All bits of misa that are reserved for future use must return zero when read.
RULE 15: The X bit in the misa Extensions field will be set if any non-standard extensions are present.
RULE 16: When the B bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports the instructions provided by the Zba, Zbb, and Zbs extensions.
RULE 17: When the M bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports all multiply and division instructions defined by the M extension.
RULE 18: If the Zmmul extension is supported, the multiply instructions it specifies are supported irrespective of the value of the M bit in misa.
RULE 19: When the S bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports supervisor mode.
RULE 20: When the U bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports user mode.
RULE 21: The E bit in misa is read-only.
RULE 22: Unless misa is all read-only zero, the E bit in misa always reads as the complement of the I bit.
RULE 23: If an execution environment supports both RV32E and RV32I, software can select RV32E by clearing the I bit in misa.
RULE 24: If an ISA feature x depends on an ISA feature y, then attempting to enable the x bit in misa while disabling the y bit results in both x and y bits being cleared in misa.
RULE 25: Setting the F bit to 0 and the D bit to 1 in misa results in both the F and D bits being cleared.
RULE 26: Setting the U bit to 0 and the S bit to 1 in misa results in both the U and S bits being cleared.
RULE 27: An attempt to write an unsupported combination of bits in misa causes those bits to be set to some supported combination.
RULE 28: If an instruction that would write misa increases IALIGN and the subsequent instruction's address is not aligned to the new IALIGN, the write to misa is suppressed, leaving misa unchanged.
RULE 29: A bit in positions 25-0 of misa set to 1 implies that the corresponding feature is implemented, but a cleared bit does not necessarily imply that the corresponding feature is not implemented.
RULE 30: In the MXL field of misa, the encoding value 1 corresponds to XLEN 32, the encoding value 2 corresponds to XLEN 64, and the encoding value 3 is reserved.
RULE 31: The encoding of the MXL field in the misa register is the same as the encoding used for the SXL and UXL fields in the mstatus register.
RULE 32: Implementations are not required to return zero from the medeleg and mideleg registers when the misa register indicates that they exist.
RULE 33: When the misa CSR is configured so that IALIGN = 32, bit mepc[1] is masked to 0 on all reads, including the implicit read performed by the MRET instruction.
RULE 34: When the misa CSR is configured so that IALIGN = 32, the bit mepc[1] remains writable despite being masked to 0 on reads.
RULE 35: Upon reset, the misa register is reset to enable the maximal set of supported extensions.
RULE 36: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of the mstateen0 CSR is read-only zero.
RULE 37: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of the hstateen0 and sstateen0 CSRs is read-only zero.
RULE 38: When the state-enable CSRs are implemented and misa.F = 0, if the FCSR bit of a controlling stateen0 CSR is zero, all floating-point instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception (or virtual-instruction exception, if relevant) as though they all access fcsr regardless of whether they actually do.
RULE 39: An implementation may allow the IALIGN field in the misa CSR to be set to either 16 or 32.
RULE 40: When the IALIGN field in misa indicates a value of 32, bit 1 of the mnepc CSR is masked on reads so that it appears as 0.
RULE 41: When the IALIGN field in misa indicates a value of 32, the implicit read of mnepc performed by the MNRET instruction also masks bit 1 to 0.
RULE 42: When the IALIGN field in misa indicates a value of 32, writes to the mnepc CSR may modify bit 1 even though reads mask it to 0.
RULE 43: An implementation may permit selection of an IALIGN value of 16 or 32 by writing the misa CSR.
RULE 44: The hypervisor extension is enabled by setting bit 7 in the misa CSR, which corresponds to the letter H.
RULE 45: When HSXLEN = 64, the VSXL field in hstatus is a WARL field whose encoding follows the same encoding rules as the MXL field of the misa register.
RULE 46: When VSXLEN equals 64, the UXL field is a WARL field whose encoding is the same as the MXL field of the misa register.

REGISTER: miselect
NUMBER: 0x350
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The CSR miselect is accessible at Machine privilege level with MRW access type.
RULE 2: When miselect is 0x30, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = iprio0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 3: When miselect is 0x3F, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = iprio15 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 4: When miselect is 0x70, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eidelivery and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 5: When miselect is 0x71, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = 0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 6: When miselect is 0x72, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eithreshold and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 7: When miselect is 0x73, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = 0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 8: When miselect is 0x7F, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = 0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 9: When miselect is 0x80, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eip0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 10: When miselect is 0xBF, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eip63 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 11: When miselect is 0xC0, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eie0 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 12: When miselect is 0xFF, the selected indirect CSR is mireg = eie63 and mireg2-mireg6 are none.
RULE 13: The value of miselect determines which register is accessed upon read or write of each machine indirect alias CSR (mireg*).
RULE 14: miselect is a WARL register.
RULE 15: The miselect register implements at least enough bits to support all implemented miselect values corresponding to the implemented extensions that utilize miselect/mireg* to indirectly access register state.
RULE 16: The miselect register may be read-only zero if no extensions implemented that utilize it.
RULE 17: Ordinarily, each mireg i accessed under a given miselect value will either access register state, access read-only zero state, or raise an illegal-instruction exception.

REGISTER: mscratch
NUMBER: 0x340
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=SCRATCH
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mscratch register has Machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: mscratch is an MXLEN-bit read/write register dedicated for use by machine mode.
RULE 3: When entry to an M-mode trap handler occurs, the value in mscratch is swapped with a user register.

REGISTER: mseccfg
NUMBER: 0x747
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..34=WPRI, 33..32=PMM, 31..11=WPRI, 10..10=MLPE, 9..9=SSEED, 8..8=USEED, 7..3=WPRI, 2..2=RLB, 1..1=MMWP, 0..0=MML
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: Implementations may implement mseccfg such that the [s,u]seed fields are a read-only constant value 0.
RULE 2: When mseccfg is implemented with the [s,u]seed fields as a read-only constant value 0, those fields read as 0 and are read-only.
RULE 3: If software writes a 1 to the [s,u]seed fields in mseccfg and subsequently reads them back, the read-back value indicates whether access to the seed CSR is enabled in U and S mode.
RULE 4: The mseccfg CSR is readable and writable in Machine mode (MRW privilege).
RULE 5: mseccfg is a 64-bit read/write register that controls security features and exists only if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented; otherwise it is reserved.
RULE 6: When mseccfg.USED = 0, any access to the seed CSR in U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When mseccfg.USED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from U-mode is allowed and all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: If the Zkr extension or U-mode is not implemented, the USEED field in mseccfg is read-only zero.
RULE 9: When mseccfg.SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR from S-/HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: When mseccfg.SSEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from S-/HS-mode is allowed and all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the Zkr extension or S-mode is not implemented, the SSEED field in mseccfg is read-only zero.
RULE 12: When the H extension is also implemented, access to the seed CSR from an HS-qualified instruction leads to a virtual-instruction exception in VS and VU modes, and all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: In machine mode, the seed CSR is always available as normal regardless of the values of the fields in mseccfg, and an attempted read without a write raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: When mseccfg.USED = 0, any seed CSR access from U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: When mseccfg.USED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal from U-mode and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 16: When mseccfg.SSEED = 0, any seed CSR access from S-/HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 17: When mseccfg.SSEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal from S-/HS-mode and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 18: When mseccfg.SSEED = 0, any seed CSR access from VS or VU mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: When mseccfg.SSEED = 1, a read-write seed CSR access from VS or VU mode raises a virtual-instruction exception and all other access conditions raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When mseccfg.RLB = 0 and any pmpcfg.L bit is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 21: When mseccfg.MMWP is set, the default PMP policy for Machine mode for memory regions without a matching PMP rule changes to denied instead of ignored.
RULE 22: When mseccfg.MML is set, the interpretation of pmpcfg.L changes so that a set pmpcfg.L marks a rule as M-mode-only and an unset pmpcfg.L marks a rule as S/U-mode-only.
RULE 23: When mseccfg.MML is set, the formerly reserved encoding pmpcfg.RW = 01 and the encoding pmpcfg.LRWX = 1111 encode a Shared-Region.
RULE 24: When mseccfg.MML is set, an M-mode-only rule is enforced on Machine mode, denied on Supervisor or User mode, and remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 25: When mseccfg.MML is set, an S/U-mode-only rule is enforced on Supervisor and User modes and denied on Machine mode.
RULE 26: When mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg.L is not set, a Shared-Region rule can be used for sharing data between M-mode and S/U-mode, is not executable, provides read/write access to M-mode, and provides read access to S/U-mode if pmpcfg.X is not set or read/write access if pmpcfg.X is set.
RULE 27: When mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg.L is set, a Shared-Region rule can be used for sharing code between M-mode and S/U-mode, is not writable, provides execute access to both M-mode and S/U-mode, and provides additional read access to M-mode if pmpcfg.X is set.
RULE 28: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg.LRWX = 1111 can be used for sharing data between M-mode and S/U-mode where both modes have read-only access, and the rule remains locked unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 29: When mseccfg.MML is set, adding a PMP rule with executable privileges that is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is not possible; such pmpcfg writes are ignored, leaving pmpcfg unchanged, and this restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 30: When mseccfg.MML is set, executing code with Machine mode privileges is only possible from memory regions with a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges; executing code from a region without a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 31: When mseccfg.MML is not set, the combination pmpcfg.RW = 01 remains reserved for future standard use.
RULE 32: The PMM field in mseccfg enables or disables pointer masking for Machine mode.
RULE 33: If the Smmpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field in mseccfg is read-only zero.
RULE 34: The PMM field in mseccfg is a WARL field whose legal values are 00 meaning pointer masking disabled (PMLEN = 0), 01 reserved, 10 meaning pointer masking enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-57 (7 on RV64), and 11 meaning pointer masking enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-48 (16 on RV64).
RULE 35: When mseccfg.MLPE = 1, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in Machine mode.
RULE 36: When mseccfg.MLPE = 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in Machine mode, the hart does not update the ELP state and it remains NO_LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 37: When mseccfg.MLPE = 0, the LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.
RULE 38: If the Zicfilp extension is implemented then the mseccfg.MLPE field MUST be reset to 0.
RULE 39: The MML field of the mseccfg register MUST be set to 0 on reset unless the platform mandates a different reset value.
RULE 40: The MMWP field of the mseccfg register MUST be set to 0 on reset unless the platform mandates a different reset value.
RULE 41: The RLB field of the mseccfg register MUST be set to 0 on reset unless the platform mandates a different reset value.
RULE 42: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is inaccessible.
RULE 43: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is inaccessible.
RULE 44: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 45: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted as execute-only.
RULE 46: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 47: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits only read operations.
RULE 48: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 49: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 50: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 51: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted as a read-only region.
RULE 52: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 53: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and execute operations.
RULE 54: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 55: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 56: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 57: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits read, write, and execute operations.
RULE 58: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is a locked inaccessible region.
RULE 59: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is a locked inaccessible region.
RULE 60: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted as a locked execute-only region.
RULE 61: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 62: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted only for execute operations because it is a locked shared code region.
RULE 63: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted only for execute operations because it is a locked shared code region.
RULE 64: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region permits read and execute operations because it is a locked shared code region.
RULE 65: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits only execute operations because it is a locked shared code region.
RULE 66: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted as a locked read-only region.
RULE 67: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 68: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted as a locked read/execute region.
RULE 69: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 70: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted as a locked read/write region.
RULE 71: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 72: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region is permitted as a locked shared data region that is read-only.
RULE 73: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted as a locked shared data region that is read-only.

REGISTER: mstateen0
NUMBER: 0x30c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0, 62..62=ENVCFG, 60..60=CSRIND, 59..59=AIA, 58..58=IMSIC, 57..57=CONTEXT, 56..56=P1P13, 55..55=SRMCFG, 54..54=CTR, 2..2=JVT, 1..1=FCSR, 0..0=C
EXTENSIONS: F, Sdtrig, Smcsrind, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssqosid, Zcmt, Zdinx, Zfinx
RULE 1: The CSR mstateen0 is a machine-mode read/write register (privilege MRW).
RULE 2: If mstateen0 prevents access to state from a less-privileged mode, an instruction in that mode that attempts to read or write the protected state raises an illegal-instruction exception, or raises a virtual-instruction exception instead when executing in VS or VU mode under the appropriate circumstances.
RULE 3: Bits in mstateen0 that are defined to control state that a hart does not implement are read-only zeros for that hart.
RULE 4: All reserved bits in mstateen0 that have not been given a defined meaning are read-only zeros.
RULE 5: For every bit in mstateen0 that is zero, whether read-only zero or set to zero, the same bit appears as read-only zero in the matching hstateen0 and sstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 6: On reset, all writable bits of mstateen0 are initialized by hardware to zero.
RULE 7: Bit 63 of mstateen0 is defined to control access to the matching sstateen0 and hstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 8: Bit 63 of mstateen0 may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and sstateen0 is entirely read-only zero; in that case machine-level software shall emulate accesses to sstateen0 from S-mode by ignoring writes and returning zero for reads.
RULE 9: A bit in sstateen0 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in mstateen0 and, if it exists, in hstateen0.
RULE 10: A bit in hstateen0 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in mstateen0.
RULE 11: The C bit in mstateen0 controls access to any and all custom state.
RULE 12: If software sets the C bit in mstateen0 but does not execute any custom instructions or access any custom state, the software must continue to execute as specified by all relevant RISC-V standards, otherwise the hardware is not standard-conforming.
RULE 13: The FCSR bit in mstateen0 controls access to fcsr for the case when floating-point instructions operate on x registers instead of f registers as specified by the Zfinx and related extensions.
RULE 14: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of mstateen0 is read-only zero.
RULE 15: When the stateen CSRs are implemented and misa.F = 0, if the FCSR bit of mstateen0 is zero then all floating-point instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception (or virtual-instruction exception, if relevant) as though they all access fcsr, regardless of whether they really do.
RULE 16: The JVT bit in mstateen0 controls access to the jvt CSR provided by the Zcmt extension.
RULE 17: The SE0 bit in mstateen0 controls access to the hstateen0, hstateen0h, and sstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 18: The ENVCFG bit in mstateen0 controls access to the henvcfg, henvcfgh, and senvcfg CSRs.
RULE 19: The CSRIND bit in mstateen0 controls access to the siselect, sireg*, vsiselect, and vsireg* CSRs provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 20: The IMSIC bit in mstateen0 controls access to the IMSIC state, including the stopei and vstopei CSRs, provided by the Ssaia extension.
RULE 21: The AIA bit in mstateen0 controls access to all state introduced by the Ssaia extension and not controlled by either the CSRIND or the IMSIC bits.
RULE 22: The CONTEXT bit in mstateen0 controls access to the scontext and hcontext CSRs provided by the Sdtrig extension.
RULE 23: The P1P13 bit in mstateen0 controls access to the hedelegh introduced by Privileged Specification Version 1.13.
RULE 24: The SRMCFG bit in mstateen0 controls access to the srmcfg CSR introduced by the Ssqosid Chapter 19 extension.
RULE 25: After reset, the writable bits of mstateen0 are zero.
RULE 26: A machine-level implementation may write the value of all ones to mstateen0.
RULE 27: The state-enable CSRs, including mstateen0, do not affect the accessibility of any state when execution is in M-mode; they affect accessibility only in privilege modes less privileged than M-mode.
RULE 28: If mstateen0[60] = 0, an attempt to access siselect, sireg*, vsiselect, or vsireg* from any privilege mode less privileged than M-mode results in an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 29: If mstateen0[60] = 1, any attempt from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect or vsireg* results in a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 30: If mstateen0[60] = 1, any attempt from VU-mode to access siselect or sireg* results in a virtual-instruction exception.
RULE 31: If hstateen0[60] = 0 and mstateen0[60] = 1, any attempt from VS-mode or VU-mode to access siselect or sireg* results in a virtual-instruction exception rather than an illegal-instruction exception, independent of the value of vsiselect or any other mstateen0 bit.
RULE 32: When the Smstateen extension is implemented and bit 60 of the CSR mstateen0 is zero, privileged modes less privileged than M-mode MUST NOT access the registers siselect, any sireg*, vsiselect, or any vsireg*.
RULE 33: When bit 60 of the CSR mstateen0 is not zero, access to a CSR is not blocked by that bit.
RULE 34: When Smstateen is implemented, the mstateen0.CTR bit controls access to CTR register state from privilege modes less privileged than M-mode.
RULE 35: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrctl raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 36: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access vsctrctl raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 37: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrdepth raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrstatus raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 39: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sireg* when siselect is in the range 0x200..0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 40: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access vsireg* when vsiselect is in the range 0x200..0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 41: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, execution of the SCTRCLR instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
