REGISTER: pmpaddr27
NUMBER: 0x3cb
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit in pmpaddr27 that is different from the G-1 bit, and the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 1 while the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 0, then the instruction reads 0 from pmpaddr27[G-1] and writes 0 back, updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr27 other than the G-1 bit, a mismatch between the underlying hardware value and the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] can cause the read value (0) to be written back, thereby updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to match the read value.
RULE 3: pmpaddr27 is a Machine-level CSR with read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr27 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: Because the pmpaddr registers are WARL, pmpaddr27 MAY be read-only zero.
RULE 6: Because all PMP CSR fields are WARL, pmpaddr27 MAY be read-only zero.
RULE 7: PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode, therefore pmpaddr27 is only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg27.A = NAPOT, the pattern of the low-order bits of pmpaddr27 encodes the size of the matched NAPOT region exactly as specified in the NAPOT range encoding table.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, pmpaddr27 provides the top address of the range while pmpaddr26 provides the bottom address.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, the PMP entry 27 matches any address y such that pmpaddr26 ≤ y < pmpaddr27, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg26.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg27.A = TOR and pmpaddr26 ≥ pmpaddr27, then PMP entry 27 matches no addresses.

RULE 13: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg27.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), reads of pmpaddr27 return all zeros in bits G-1 down to 0.
RULE 14: The low bits of pmpaddr27 masked by granularity (bits G-1 down to 0) are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 15: The physical bit pmpaddr27[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg27.A is changed between NAPOT and OFF/TOR modes, even though the read value of pmpaddr27 may change.
RULE 16: If PMP entry 27 is locked, writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 17: The L bit for entry 27 indicates that the PMP entry is locked, and therefore writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 18: Setting the L bit for entry 27 locks the PMP entry even when the A field is set to OFF, and consequently writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 19: For the PMP rule that uses pmpaddr27 to be a valid protected physical memory region, the field pmpcfg27.A must not be OFF.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg27.A is TOR, then the value in pmpaddr26 must be strictly less than the value in pmpaddr27.

REGISTER: pmpaddr28
NUMBER: 0x3cc
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: A CSRRW instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the old value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and writes the initial value in rs1 to pmpaddr28.
RULE 2: If a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 has rd = x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr28 and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.
RULE 3: A CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr28.
RULE 4: A CSRRS instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that sets corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 5: A CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that clears corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 6: When executing CSRRS or CSRRC on pmpaddr28, any bits that read as a different value from their underlying value may be modified even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1.
RULE 7: If pmpaddr28[G-1] has an underlying value of 1 but reads as 0, executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr28 to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr28[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 8: For CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28, if rs1 = x0, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28 at all, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 9: CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 always read pmpaddr28 and cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 10: If rs1 specifies a register other than x0 and that register holds a zero value, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr28 will not trigger any per-field side effects but will trigger any side effects caused by writing to the entire pmpaddr28.
RULE 11: The CSRRWI, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI immediate-form instructions targeting pmpaddr28 behave as their register-operand counterparts, using a zero-extended 5-bit immediate instead of rs1.
RULE 12: If a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 has an immediate field uimm[4:0] equal to zero, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 13: For a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd = x0, the instruction does not read pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 14: For a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 15: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 16: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 17: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd = x0, the instruction does not read pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 18: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 19: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm = 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 20: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm != 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 21: No standard CSR, including pmpaddr28, has side effects on field writes.
RULE 22: pmpaddr28 is not among the CSRs that are automatically modified as side effects of instruction execution, so no automatic update side effect applies to pmpaddr28.
RULE 23: pmpaddr28 is a WARL field.
RULE 24: Software may write any value to pmpaddr28.
RULE 25: The hardware may modify the value written to pmpaddr28.
RULE 26: pmpaddr28 may read as zero if the implementation provides a read-only zero value.
RULE 27: pmpaddr28 is accessible only in machine mode.
RULE 28: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 0, the entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 29: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 1, the entry uses TOR mode with pmpaddr28 serving as the top of the address range.
RULE 30: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 2, the entry uses NA4 mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a 4-byte range.
RULE 31: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 3, the entry uses NAPOT mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a naturally aligned power-of-two range.
RULE 32: If the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr27 ≤ y < pmpaddr28, irrespective of the value of the preceding configuration register.
RULE 33: If pmpaddr27 ≥ pmpaddr28 and the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 34: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NA4, the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 encode a 4-byte range as defined by the NA4 encoding.
RULE 35: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yyy0, the entry matches an 8-byte range.
RULE 36: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yy01, the entry matches a 16-byte range.
RULE 37: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…y011, the entry matches a 32-byte range.
RULE 38: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yy01…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 39: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern y011…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 40: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 0111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 41: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 1111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 42: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode must not be selected for the entry whose address register is pmpaddr28.
RULE 43: When G ≥ 2 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set, bits pmpaddr28[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 44: When G ≥ 1 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is clear, bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 45: Bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for the entry that contains pmpaddr28.
RULE 46: Changing the high bit of the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 changes the value read from pmpaddr28 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr28[G-1] retains its original value when the configuration is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 47: Writes to pmpaddr28 are ignored when PMP entry 28 is locked.
RULE 48: The L bit of PMP entry 28 indicates that the entry is locked, causing writes to the configuration register and associated address registers, including pmpaddr28, to be ignored.
RULE 49: When pmpaddr28 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset.

REGISTER: pmpaddr29
NUMBER: 0x3cd
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: When the CSR pmpaddr29 is read, bit G-1 may have an underlying stored value of 1 but be observed as 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read of pmpaddr29[G-1] to return 0.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read value 0 to be written back to pmpaddr29[G-1], updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr29[G-1] to 0.

RULE 5: For RV64, pmpaddr29 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: pmpaddr29 is a WARL field because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: pmpaddr29 may be read-only zero as all PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 8: Reads or writes of pmpaddr29 are only permitted when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 9: If the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 has its A field set to NA4, then the value stored in pmpaddr29 is of the form yyyy…yyyy and pmpaddr29 matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with a single zero (…0), then pmpaddr29 matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …01, then pmpaddr29 matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …011, then pmpaddr29 matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 14: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then pmpaddr29 defines the top of the address range and the preceding address register pmpaddr28 defines the bottom of the address range.
RULE 15: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then entry 29 matches any address y such that pmpaddr28 ≤ y < pmpaddr29, irrespective of the value of the configuration register for entry 28.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr28 ≥ pmpaddr29 and the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is TOR, then entry 29 matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 2 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 1 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-1:0] read as all zeros.

RULE 20: Although changing bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 alters the value read from pmpaddr29, it does not modify the underlying stored bits, and specifically bit pmpaddr29[G-1] retains its original stored value when the A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmp0cfg, writing all ones to pmpaddr29, and then reading back pmpaddr29; the index G of the least-significant set bit in the read value indicates that the granularity is 2^G + 2 bytes.
RULE 22: If the L bit of PMP entry 29 is set, writes to pmpaddr29 are ignored.
RULE 23: Once the L bit of PMP entry 29 has been set, the lock on pmpaddr29 persists until a hart reset occurs.
RULE 24: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 29 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr29 to be ignored regardless of the value of the A field in pmp29 cfg.

RULE 1: Because the pmpaddr registers are WARL, pmpaddr36 may be read-only zero.

RULE 3: PMP CSRs are only accessible in machine mode, therefore pmpaddr36 can be accessed only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 4: If PMP entry 36 is locked, writes to pmpaddr36 are ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr37
NUMBER: 0x3d5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr37 may have an underlying value of 1 but read as 0.
RULE 2: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit other than the top-most PMP address bit of pmpaddr37, the hardware must read the current read value of pmpaddr37[G-1] (which may be 0 even if the underlying value is 1), must write that read value back, and must update the underlying value of that bit to match the read value.
RULE 3: CSRRS and CSRRC always read pmpaddr37 and cause any read side effects defined for pmpaddr37 regardless of the rs1 and rd fields.
RULE 4: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 = x0 must not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 5: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 ≠ x0 must write to pmpaddr37 and must trigger side effects for any fields whose corresponding bits are set in rs1.
RULE 6: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 ≠ x0 and with the source register containing zero must not trigger per-field side effects on pmpaddr37 but must trigger any side effects associated with writing the entire CSR.
RULE 7: For any CSRRS or CSRRC targeting pmpaddr37, the CSR is always read and it is written only when rs1 ≠ x0.
RULE 8: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] = 0 shall not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 9: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] ≠ 0 must read and write pmpaddr37 and must follow the same per-field side-effect rules as CSRRS or CSRRC.
RULE 10: A CSRRW targeting pmpaddr37 with rs1 = x0 must write the value 0 into pmpaddr37.
RULE 11: The architectural privilege level for pmpaddr37 is MRW (Machine-Read/Write).
RULE 12: Reads or writes to the register pmpaddr37 MUST be performed only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 13: Each field of the register pmpaddr37 is a WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) field and the register MAY read back as zero regardless of the value written.
RULE 14: When executing on an RV64 hart, the value written to the register pmpaddr37 supplies bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address for PMP entry 37.
RULE 15: Physical-address bits that are not implemented on a particular implementation affect the legal values that can be written to the register pmpaddr37, and writes of illegal values MAY be silently masked or cause the register to read back a different legal value.
RULE 16: With pmpcfg37.A = 2 (NA4), the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 are all ones and represent a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 0, the encoded region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 18: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 01, the encoded region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 19: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 011, the encoded region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 20: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and all low-order bits of pmpaddr37 set to 1, the encoded region size is 2^{XLEN}+3 bytes.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg37.A = TOR, pmpaddr37 serves as the top bound of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr36 ≤ y < pmpaddr37, regardless of the value of pmpcfg36.
RULE 22: If pmpaddr36 ≥ pmpaddr37 and pmpcfg37.A = TOR, then PMP entry 37 matches no addresses.
RULE 23: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 24: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 25: Bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 26: Changing pmpcfg37.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr37 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr37[G-1] retains its original value when the mode is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 27: If the L bit in pmpcfg37 is set, writes to pmpaddr37 are ignored.
RULE 28: The lock of PMP entry 37, which governs pmpaddr37, remains in effect until the hart is reset.
RULE 29: The architectural rule that a locked PMP entry causes writes to its pmpaddr register to be ignored applies to entry 37, so the L bit in pmpcfg37 directly causes the write-ignore behavior for pmpaddr37.
RULE 30: A PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpcfg37.A is not OFF.
RULE 31: If pmpcfg37.A TOR, then a PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpaddr36 is less than pmpaddr37.

REGISTER: pmpaddr38

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The register pmpaddr38 may have an underlying bit value that differs from the value read, such that pmpaddr38[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.

REGISTER: pmpaddr4

WIDTH: MXLEN

RULE 1: pmpaddr4[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.

RULE 3: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that modifies a bit other than G-1 of pmpaddr4 will cause a read of 0 from pmpaddr4[G-1] and will write back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr4[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr4 and shall not cause any side effects that would occur on a CSR write, nor shall it raise an illegal-instruction exception on a read-only pmpaddr4.
RULE 5: A CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr4 shall always read pmpaddr4 and shall cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 6: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 specifying a register other than x0 that contains the value zero, the instruction will not action any per-field side effects but will action any side effects caused by writing the entire pmpaddr4.
RULE 7: A CSRRW instruction that accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 equal to x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr4.
RULE 8: When a CSRRW instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr4 but shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 9: When a CSRRW instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 10: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 11: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 12: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr4 but shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 13: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 14: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 15: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is non-zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 16: When pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRW or CSRRWI instruction, side effects for all fields of pmpaddr4 shall be enacted.
RULE 17: When pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRS, CSRRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI instruction, side effects shall be enacted only for those fields of pmpaddr4 whose corresponding bits are set in the rs1 register or uimm argument.
RULE 18: pmpaddr4 is a WARL register.
RULE 19: Any field of pmpaddr4 may be read-only zero.
RULE 20: pmpaddr4 can be accessed only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg4.A = NAPOT, bits pmpaddr4 encode the NAPOT range size as follows: pattern …yyy0 selects an 8-byte range, …yy01 selects a 16-byte range, …y011 selects a 32-byte range, …yy01…1111 selects a 2 XLEN-byte range, …y011…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+1-byte range, 0111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+2-byte range, and 1111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+3-byte range.

RULE 23: When pmpcfg4.A = TOR, pmpaddr4 defines the top address of the TOR range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr3 ≤ y < pmpaddr4, irrespective of pmpcfg3.
RULE 24: If pmpaddr3 ≥ pmpaddr4 and pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then PMP entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 25: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 26: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 27: Bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.

RULE 29: When the granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable, so pmpaddr4 cannot be used with pmpcfg4.A = 2 (NA4) in such implementations.
RULE 30: If PMP entry 4 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr4 has no effect and is ignored.
RULE 31: If PMP entry 4 is locked and its configuration register pmp4 cfg specifies address-matching mode TOR, any write to the preceding address register pmpaddr4-1 is ignored.
RULE 32: Setting the L bit in pmp4 cfg locks PMP entry 4 regardless of the value of pmp4 cfg.A (including OFF), causing subsequent writes to pmpaddr4 to be ignored.
RULE 33: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is set, the R, W, and X permission checks associated with entry 4 are enforced for M-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 as well as for S- and U-mode accesses.
RULE 34: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is clear, M-mode accesses that match entry 4 as defined by pmpaddr4 succeed irrespective of the R, W, and X permission bits, while S- and U-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 are still subject to those permission checks.
RULE 35: pmpaddr3 MUST be less than pmpaddr4 when the address-matching mode field A of pmpcfg4 is TOR.

RULE 9: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with a single 0 (...0), then the PMP entry matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with the bits 01 (...01), then the PMP entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with the bits 011 (...011), then the PMP entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form yy01...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form y011...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form 0111...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form 1111...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg43.A = TOR, then pmpaddr43 defines the upper bound of the address range so that the PMP entry matches any address y satisfying pmpaddr42 ≤ y < pmpaddr43, independent of pmpcfg42.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg43.A = TOR and pmpaddr42 ≥ pmpaddr43, then the PMP entry 43 matches no addresses.
RULE 18: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg43.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then the bits pmpaddr43[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg43.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then the bits pmpaddr43[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: The bits pmpaddr43[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg43.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr43 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and the bit pmpaddr43[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg43.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 43 is locked, any write to pmpaddr43 is ignored.
RULE 23: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 43 locks the entry, causing writes to pmpaddr43 to be ignored.
RULE 24: A locked PMP entry 43 remains locked until a hart reset, so the ignore-write behavior for pmpaddr43 persists until a hart reset.
RULE 25: Setting the L bit locks PMP entry 43 even when its A field is OFF, and consequently writes to pmpaddr43 are ignored when A=OFF.

RULE 2: The pmpaddr51[G-1] field may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that field returns 0.
RULE 3: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr51 to modify a bit other than pmpaddr51[G-1] causes a 0 to be read from pmpaddr51[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr51[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: The privilege level for pmpaddr51 is MRW, meaning machine-read/write access.
RULE 5: pmpaddr51 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address when the implementation is RV64.
RULE 6: pmpaddr51 is a WARL register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: pmpaddr51 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 8: The A field of pmpcfg51 encodes the address-matching mode of pmpaddr51, where OFF = 0, TOR = 1, NA4 = 2, and NAPOT = 3.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg51.A is NA4 or NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr51 encode the size of the address range according to the pattern defined in Table 24.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg51.A is TOR, pmpaddr51 provides the top address of the PMP entry's address range.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg51.A is TOR, the PMP entry matches any address y satisfying pmpaddr50 ≤ y < pmpaddr51, independent of pmpcfg50.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg51.A is TOR and pmpaddr50 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr51, then the PMP entry matches no addresses.
RULE 13: When the PMP granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg51.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr51[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 14: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg51.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr51[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 15: Bits pmpaddr51[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 16: Changing pmpcfg51.A[1] modifies the value read from pmpaddr51 but does not alter the underlying stored value of pmpaddr51.
RULE 17: The bit pmpaddr51[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg51.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 18: If PMP entry 51 is locked, writes to pmpaddr51 are ignored.
RULE 19: The L bit of PMP entry 51 indicates that the entry is locked, and therefore writes to pmpaddr51 are ignored.
RULE 20: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 51 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr51 to be ignored even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 21: When the L bit of PMP entry 51 is set, the R, W, and X permissions associated with pmpaddr51 are enforced for all privilege modes; when the L bit is clear, any M-mode access that matches pmpaddr51 succeeds and the R, W, and X permissions apply only to S-mode and U-mode accesses.
RULE 22: For the PMP entry that uses pmpaddr51, the associated pmpcfg[51].A field MUST NOT be OFF for the entry to encode a valid protected physical memory region.
RULE 23: If the associated pmpcfg[51].A field is TOR then pmpaddr50 MUST be less than pmpaddr51.

REGISTER: pmpaddr52
NUMBER: 0x3e4
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr52[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of the register returns 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr52[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: In RV64, pmpaddr52 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 4: pmpaddr52 is a WARL register.
RULE 5: pmpaddr52 may be read-only zero.
RULE 6: pmpaddr52 can be accessed only when the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 7: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg52.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr52[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 8: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg52.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr52[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 9: Bits pmpaddr52[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 10: Changing pmpcfg52.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr52.
RULE 11: Changing pmpcfg52.A[1] does not affect the underlying stored value in pmpaddr52, and pmpaddr52[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg52.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.
RULE 12: If PMP entry 52 is locked, any write to the pmpaddr52 register must be ignored.
RULE 13: When the L bit of PMP entry 52 is set, writes to the pmpaddr52 register are ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr53
NUMBER: 0x3e5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr53[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that bit returns 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr53, any bit that reads as a value different from its underlying value may be modified even if the corresponding bit in rs1 is zero.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction on pmpaddr53 to modify a bit other than G-1 will cause a read of pmpaddr53[G-1] that returns 0 and will subsequently write back 0, updating its underlying value to 0.
RULE 4: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr53 always reads pmpaddr53 and triggers any read-side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 5: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 equals x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 but does not write it.
RULE 6: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 is not x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 and writes it, subject to the per-field side-effect rules.
RULE 7: The privilege of pmpaddr53 is MRW, allowing read and write access only in machine mode.
RULE 8: pmpaddr53 is a WARL register.
RULE 9: pmpaddr53 may contain any value that is legal for the implementation.
RULE 10: Reads of pmpaddr53 may return zero even if written with a non-zero value.
RULE 11: pmpaddr53 can be read only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 12: pmpaddr53 can be written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 13: When a PMP setting that additionally uses the preceding address register applies to PMP entry 53, the behavior of pmpaddr53 can be directly affected by the value in pmpaddr52.
RULE 14: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is 0 (OFF), the entry is disabled and matches no addresses, and the value stored in pmpaddr53 is irrelevant for matching.
RULE 15: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is set to TOR, pmpaddr53 forms the top of the address range for entry 53.
RULE 16: In TOR mode, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr52 <= y < pmpaddr53, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg52.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr52 >= pmpaddr53 and pmpcfg53.A = TOR, then PMP entry 53 matches no addresses.
RULE 18: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is NA4, the entire contents of pmpaddr53 are used as a 4-byte NAPOT range aligned to a four-byte boundary, and the low-order bits are not interpreted for size.
RULE 19: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr53 encode the size of the region according to the specified patterns.
RULE 20: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 are all 1, the NAPOT region size is 4 bytes.
RULE 21: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 0, the NAPOT region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 22: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 01, the NAPOT region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 23: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 011, the NAPOT region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 24: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...yy01...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN bytes.
RULE 25: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...y011...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+1 bytes.
RULE 26: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...0111...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+2 bytes.
RULE 27: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern ...1111...1111, the NAPOT region size is 2*XLEN+3 bytes.
RULE 28: If G >= 2 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is set (entry 53 is in NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr53[G-2:0] read as all ones regardless of their stored values.
RULE 29: If G >= 1 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is clear (entry 53 is OFF or TOR), bits pmpaddr53[G-1:0] read as all zeros and these bits do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 30: Changing pmpcfg53.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr53 but does not change the underlying value stored in the register.
RULE 31: Bit pmpaddr53[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg53.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 32: If PMP entry 53 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr53 is ignored.
RULE 33: When the L bit of PMP entry 53 is set, writes to the address register pmpaddr53 are ignored.
RULE 34: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 53 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr53 to be ignored even if the A field of pmpcfg53 is OFF.
RULE 35: A locked PMP entry 53, and therefore its address register pmpaddr53, remains locked and write-ignored until the hart is reset.

REGISTER: pmpaddr54
NUMBER: 0x3e6
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr54 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the hart is RV64, the pmpaddr54 register encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 3: Implementations are not required to implement all physical address bits for the pmpaddr54 register.
RULE 4: The pmpaddr54 register is WARL (Write Any Values, Read Legal).
RULE 5: The pmpaddr54 register may be read-only zero.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg54.A = 0 (OFF), the PMP entry is disabled and pmpaddr54 matches no addresses.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg54.A = 1 (TOR), pmpaddr54 forms the top of the address range, the preceding pmpaddr53 forms the bottom, and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr53 ≤ y < pmpaddr54, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg53.
RULE 8: If pmpaddr53 ≥ pmpaddr54 and pmpcfg54.A = 1 (TOR), then pmpaddr54 matches no addresses.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg54.A = 2 (NA4), pmpaddr54 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range, with its value having the form yyyy…yyyy.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg54.A = 3 (NAPOT), pmpaddr54 uses its low-order bits to encode the size of the range as specified in Table 24.
RULE 11: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern yyyy…yyy0, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 8 bytes.
RULE 12: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern yyyy…yy01, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 16 bytes.
RULE 13: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern yyyy…y011, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 32 bytes.
RULE 14: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern yy01…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN bytes.
RULE 15: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern y011…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN+1 bytes.
RULE 16: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern 0111…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN+2 bytes.
RULE 17: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr54 match the pattern 1111…1111, then the NAPOT range size encoded by pmpaddr54 is 2 XLEN+3 bytes.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg54.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr54[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg54.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr54[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr54[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg54.A[1] (switching between NAPOT and TOR/OFF) affects the value read from pmpaddr54 but does not affect the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr54[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg54.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 54 is locked (the L bit for entry 54 is set), writes to pmpaddr54 are ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr55
NUMBER: 0x3e7
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The G-1 bit of pmpaddr55 (pmpaddr55[G-1]) may have an underlying stored value of 1 while being read as 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies any bit of pmpaddr55 other than G-1 MUST cause the value read from pmpaddr55[G-1] (which may be 0) to be written back to the register, thereby updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr55[G-1] to the value that was read.
RULE 3: pmpaddr55 has privilege level MRW (Machine-Read/Write).
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr55 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr55 is a WARL (Write-Any-Read-Legal) register.
RULE 6: pmpaddr55 may be read-only zero.
RULE 7: pmpaddr55 may implement only a subset of the address bits that it encodes.
RULE 8: pmpaddr55 can be read only while the hart is in machine mode.
RULE 9: pmpaddr55 can be written only while the hart is in machine mode.
RULE 10: When the configuration register field A for PMP entry 55 is 0 (OFF), the entry that uses pmpaddr55 is disabled and matches no addresses.

RULE 23: When the granularity G is at least 1 and the high bit A[1] of the configuration register for entry 55 is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr55[G-1:0] read as all zeros.

RULE 28: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is set, the R, W, and X permission bits associated with pmpaddr55 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 29: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is clear, any machine-mode access that matches the address range defined by pmpaddr55 succeeds regardless of the R, W, and X permission bits.
RULE 30: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is clear, the R, W, and X permission bits associated with pmpaddr55 apply only to supervisor and user mode accesses.
RULE 31: The contents of pmpaddr55 together with pmpcfg55 encode a valid protected physical memory region only when pmpcfg55.A is not OFF.
RULE 32: When pmpcfg55.A equals TOR, the address stored in pmpaddr54 must be less than the address stored in pmpaddr55.

RULE 21: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg58.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr58[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 22: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg58.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr58[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 23: Bits pmpaddr58[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 24: Changing pmpcfg58.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr58 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr58[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg58.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 25: The contents of pmpcfg58 and its associated pmpaddr58 registers encode a protected physical memory region when pmpcfg58.A is not OFF.
RULE 26: If pmpcfg58.A equals TOR then pmpaddr57 must be less than pmpaddr58.
RULE 27: If the pmpcfg58.L bit is set then the PMP entry containing pmpaddr58 is a Locked entry.

REGISTER: pmpaddr59
NUMBER: 0x3eb
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr59 register may have an underlying stored value of 1 for its most-significant address bit G-1 while a read of pmpaddr59 returns 0 for that bit.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies any bit of pmpaddr59 other than G-1 will cause the read of pmpaddr59 to return 0 for bit G-1 and will cause that 0 to be written back, updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr59[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: The underlying stored value of pmpaddr59[G-1] can be changed indirectly by a CSRRC or CSRRS operation that targets a different bit of pmpaddr59, even though the operation's bit-mask does not include G-1.
RULE 4: pmpaddr59 is a Machine-level CSR with read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 5: On an RV64 hart, pmpaddr59 holds bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address used for PMP entry 59.
RULE 6: The fields of pmpaddr59 are WARL and may read back as zero.
RULE 7: pmpaddr59 may be read or written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 8: If an implementation provides fewer than 60 PMP entries, pmpaddr59 is not implemented.
RULE 9: PMP entry 60 may use pmpaddr59 as the address register that influences entry 60's behavior.
RULE 10: Bits of pmpaddr59 that correspond to physical address bits not implemented by the hardware may be ignored or forced to zero.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg59.A = NA4 then the value of pmpaddr59 is of the form yyyy…yyyy and PMP entry 59 matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg59.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr59 are …0 then PMP entry 59 matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg59.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr59 are …01 then PMP entry 59 matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg59.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr59 are …011 then PMP entry 59 matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg59.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr59 follow any of the patterns shown in the remaining rows of Table 24 (e.g., yy01…1111, y011…1111, 0111…1111, 1111…1111) then PMP entry 59 matches the corresponding NAPOT range size (2 XLEN-byte, 2 XLEN+1-byte, 2 XLEN+2-byte, or 2 XLEN+3-byte).
RULE 16: If pmpcfg59.A = TOR then PMP entry 59 matches any address y such that pmpaddr58 ≤ y < pmpaddr59 irrespective of the value of pmpcfg58.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr58 ≥ pmpaddr59 and pmpcfg59.A = TOR then PMP entry 59 matches no addresses.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg59.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode) then bits pmpaddr59[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg59.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode) then bits pmpaddr59[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr59[G-1:0] do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg59.A[1] alters the value read from pmpaddr59 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr59[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg59.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 59 is locked, writes to pmpaddr59 are ignored.
RULE 23: If PMP entry 59 is locked and pmp59 cfg.A is set to TOR, writes to pmpaddr58 are ignored, and writes to pmpaddr59 are also ignored because the entry is locked.
RULE 24: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 59 locks the entry, which causes writes to pmpaddr59 to be ignored even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 25: When the L bit for PMP entry 59 is set, the R/W/X permissions apply to all privilege modes for accesses whose address matches the range specified by pmpaddr59, and when the L bit is clear any M-mode access matching the address range specified by pmpaddr59 succeeds with R/W/X permissions applying only to S and U modes.

REGISTER: pmpaddr6
NUMBER: 0x3b6
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr6 register contains a field named pmpaddr6[G-1] that may have an underlying value of 1 while being read as 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit other than pmpaddr6[G-1], the instruction reads a value of 0 from pmpaddr6[G-1].
RULE 3: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit other than pmpaddr6[G-1], the instruction writes the read value 0 back to pmpaddr6[G-1], causing the underlying value of pmpaddr6[G-1] to become 0.
RULE 4: pmpaddr6 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr6 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: Because not all physical address bits may be implemented, the pmpaddr6 register is WARL (write-any-legal-value, read-as-legal-value).
RULE 7: All PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero, therefore pmpaddr6 is WARL and may read as zero.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg6.A = NA4 or NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr6 encode the size of the range according to Table 24 (e.g., "yyyy…yyy0" for an 8-byte NAPOT range, "yyyy…yy01" for a 16-byte NAPOT range, …, "1111…1111" for a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range).
RULE 9: When pmpcfg6.A = TOR, pmpaddr6 defines the top of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr5 ≤ y < pmpaddr6, irrespective of pmpcfg5.A.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg6.A = TOR and pmpaddr5 ≥ pmpaddr6, then PMP entry 6 matches no addresses.
RULE 11: When the granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg6.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr6[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 12: When the granularity G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg6.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg6.A = TOR, bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg6.A[1] is changed, the underlying stored value of pmpaddr6[G-1] retains its original value, while the value read from pmpaddr6 may change according to the read-value rules.
RULE 15: If the L bit of PMP entry 6 is set, writes to pmpaddr6 MUST be ignored.
RULE 16: A locked PMP entry 6 MUST remain locked until a hart reset, causing writes to pmpaddr6 to continue to be ignored until that reset.
RULE 17: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 6 MUST lock the entry, which controls pmpaddr6 behavior, regardless of the A field value.

REGISTER: pmpaddr60
NUMBER: 0x3ec
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr60 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 2: pmpaddr60 is a WARL register because implementations may not implement all physical address bits.
RULE 3: pmpaddr60 may be read-only zero if the corresponding physical address bits are not implemented.
RULE 4: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 0, the entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 5: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 1 (TOR), pmpaddr60 provides the top of the address range.
RULE 6: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 2 (NA4), the entry matches a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 7: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 3 (NAPOT), the entry matches a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 8: If the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that the value in the preceding PMP address register is ≤ y < pmpaddr60.
RULE 9: If the value in the preceding PMP address register is greater than or equal to pmpaddr60 and the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 10: If pmpaddr60 contains a pattern of all y bits and the associated A field is NA4, the entry matches a four-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpaddr60 ends with a single 0 bit (pattern yyyy…yyy0) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches an eight-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpaddr60 ends with the bit pattern 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a sixteen-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr60 ends with the bit pattern 011 (pattern yyyy…y011) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a thirty-two-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern yy01…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern y011…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern 0111…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern 1111…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 18: When the granularity G is at least 2 and the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr60[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When the granularity G is at least 1 and the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr60[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr60[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 alters the value read from pmpaddr60 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and the bit pmpaddr60[G-1] retains its original value when the A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 60 is locked, writes to pmpaddr60 are ignored.
RULE 23: The L bit of PMP entry 60 indicates that writes to pmpaddr60 are ignored.
RULE 24: Once PMP entry 60 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset, so pmpaddr60 stays locked.
RULE 25: Setting the L bit locks PMP entry 60 (and thus pmpaddr60) even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 26: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is set, the R/W/X permissions associated with pmpaddr60 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 27: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is clear, any M-mode access matching pmpaddr60 will succeed and the R/W/X permissions apply only to S and U modes.

REGISTER: pmpaddr61
NUMBER: 0x3ed
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr61 register [G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read returns 0.

RULE 3: When pmpcfg61.A is set to TOR, pmpaddr61 defines the top address of the TOR-matched range, with pmpaddr60 defining the bottom address.

RULE 5: If pmpaddr60 ≥ pmpaddr61 while pmpcfg61.A is set to TOR, entry 61 matches no addresses.

RULE 7: For a 4-byte NAPOT range, the low-order bits of pmpaddr61 are all zero.
RULE 8: For an 8-byte NAPOT range, the least significant bit of pmpaddr61 is zero and the next least significant bit is one.
RULE 9: For a 16-byte NAPOT range, the two least significant bits of pmpaddr61 are "01".
RULE 10: The NAPOT encoding pattern continues such that the maximum 2^(XLEN+3)-byte range is represented by pmpaddr61 having all bits set to one.
RULE 11: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg61.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr61[G-2:0] read as all ones.

RULE 16: If PMP entry 61 is locked, any write to pmpaddr61 is ignored.
RULE 17: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 61 locks the entry even when the A field is OFF, causing writes to pmpaddr61 to be ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr62
NUMBER: 0x3ee
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr62 is a CSR whose underlying value may differ from the value read, for example the underlying value may be 1 while the CSR reads 0.
RULE 2: Any bits of pmpaddr62 that read as a different value from their underlying value may be modified by CSRRS or CSRRC instructions even if the corresponding bit is not set in rs1.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr62 to modify a different bit causes the mismatched read value to be read from pmpaddr62.
RULE 4: After the mismatched read value is obtained, it is written back to pmpaddr62, updating the underlying value to that read value.
RULE 5: In RV64, pmpaddr62 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: pmpaddr62 is a WARL register and may read as zero regardless of the value written.
RULE 7: pmpaddr62 may be read or written only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 8: pmpaddr62 exists only in implementations that provide 64 PMP entries and is absent in implementations that provide 0 or 16 PMP entries.
RULE 9: In configurations where preceding-address usage applies, the address value in pmpaddr62 may be used by the PMP entry that follows it (entry 63).
RULE 10: If the L bit of PMP entry 62 is set, any write to pmpaddr62 MUST be ignored.
RULE 11: If PMP entry 62 is locked, writes to pmpaddr62 MUST be ignored.
RULE 12: Once PMP entry 62 becomes locked, it remains locked until a hart reset, so pmpaddr62 stays locked until that reset.
RULE 13: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 62 locks the entry even when its A field is OFF, causing writes to pmpaddr62 to be ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr63
NUMBER: 0x3ef
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr63 other than bit G-1, the instruction shall read pmpaddr63, and if bit G-1 reads as a value different from its underlying stored value, the instruction shall write back that read value for bit G-1, thereby updating the underlying value of bit G-1 to the read value.
RULE 2: Bit G-1 of pmpaddr63 may be stored as 1 but read as 0.
RULE 3: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr63 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall cause any read side effects associated with pmpaddr63 regardless of the values in rs1 or rd.
RULE 4: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 targets pmpaddr63, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr63, shall not cause any write-side effects on pmpaddr63, and shall not raise an illegal-instruction exception for a read-only access to pmpaddr63.
RULE 5: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 not equal to x0 shall both read pmpaddr63 and write pmpaddr63.
RULE 6: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall not write pmpaddr63.
RULE 7: The pmpaddr63 CSR has privilege MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 8: In RV64 systems, pmpaddr63 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 9: pmpaddr63 is a WARL field and may be read-only zero.
RULE 10: pmpaddr63 may be accessed (read or written) only while executing in M-mode.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg63.A = OFF, pmpaddr63 defines a null (disabled) region.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR, pmpaddr63 forms the top address of the range, with pmpaddr62 as the bottom address.
RULE 13: When pmpcfg63.A = TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr62 ≤ y < pmpaddr63, irrespective of pmpcfg62.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR and the entry is the first PMP entry, then zero is used as the lower bound and the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr63.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr62 ≥ pmpaddr63 and pmpcfg63.A = TOR, then the entry using pmpaddr63 matches no addresses.
RULE 16: pmpaddr63 MUST NOT be used to represent the address 2^XLEN+2 as the top of a TOR range, and therefore a TOR entry using pmpaddr63 cannot grant access to the uppermost word of memory.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg63.A = NA4, pmpaddr63 specifies a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 0, then pmpaddr63 encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 01, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 011, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 21: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern yy01…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 22: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern y011…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 23: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 0111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 1111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 25: When G ≥ 1, pmpaddr63 MUST NOT be used in NA4 mode.
RULE 26: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 27: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 28: Bits pmpaddr63[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 29: Changing pmpcfg63.A[1] does not modify the stored value of bit pmpaddr63[G-1]; the original bit value is retained across mode changes.
RULE 30: If the L bit of PMP entry 63 is set, any write to pmpaddr63 is ignored.
RULE 31: Once the L bit of PMP entry 63 is set, the lock remains in effect until a hart reset, causing writes to pmpaddr63 to continue to be ignored.
